body.title: The Engraver's Message
body.body:
*My most esteemed and illustrious Lord,*

May this missive find Your Excellency in great health and illuminated by the High Graces. This note is to advise you that the project has been completed as per my Lord’s exacting specifications. In addition to the illustration, supporting documentation with itemized deliverables and additional notes on the production of the diagram are further provided.

In regards to the matter concerning the young workshop assistant, it has been impressed upon him that he is to speak to no soul on the work he has carried out. I assure Your Grace that the boy is as discrete as he is talented, and I can vouch for his character. He’s also smart enough to realize the consequences of a tactless tongue and appreciate the importance of this work for the betterment of Man.

One last matter shall conclude the object of my letter, and it is in regards to an unfamiliar lady who showed up at my shop with images similar to the ones used in this project. Dressed in leather and blue silk, she was interested in assessing the accuracy of her diagrams, as well as their possible provenance. *We gave no counsel whatsoever to her in these matters.* I am but a simple engraver and not a formulaic man, but in my estimation, this young lady seems to have intimate knowledge of the illustrated subjects. Where she may have come by such knowledge and materials, I know not. My astute assistant penned her likeness, as can be seen in the accompanying folio. I bring special attention to the graphical design of the ring on her left hand, which appears to be from a Guild unfamiliar to our city. 

I hope this information is useful, and I am at your disposal should more be required of my services.

May the light of Providence continue shining on Your Lordship. 

*I am as ever
Your Humble Servant
Hippolytus of Westdale Hills* 

The earliest known date that Leonardo Da Vinci may have become a heretic was 1507-08. At this time, the Church had much more power than it does now. If they didn’t like what you were up to, then you could get in trouble with the inquisition. It was at this point when Leonardo embarked in one the most astonishing projects of his life that consisted of going into morgues to dissect and sketch human bodies. He painstakingly, and with scalpel in hand, used his skills to draw diagrams of human bodies that are some of the most incredible images when one considers the context in which they were produced.

Leonardo approached the gruesome task not as a medieval physician speaking of humours, vital forces, and other *metaphysical* terms but used plain language borne of his engineering and artistic endeavors. His findings were amazing. He compared the bodies of a diseased old man and a boy at a hospital to record the differences. He delved into the vascular system finding that ‘weakness caused by a lack of blood’ made the arteries ‘very dry, thin, and withered… in addition to the thickening of the walls, these vessels grow in length.’ (Nicholls, 2004). He studied the heart and corroborated the Aristotelian view that the heart is where ‘the tree of the vessels grow.’ Hounded and ‘hindered’ by the Church for his rather grim research, Da Vinci’s observations and more importantly, his anatomical illustrations were kept hidden for centuries and did not influence anyone, as far as we know.

Like the existence of the Antikythera mechanism, these historical tidbits keep me up at night. It makes me wonder how much more different our history would have been if we had just been more open to the reception of scientific novelty.

I was recently testing AI’s ability to create accurate scientific illustrations and generated an illustration of the ossicles (malleus, incus, and stapes), which are the smallest bones in our bodies and help us process sound. To my astonishment, the software created an accurate representation of these bones. It also generated Latin text to fill up the white space in the illustration. This floored me. I am no language expert or metaphysician, but the text appears to accurately describe the nature of the ossicles in Latin. 😮

The illustration reminded me of Da Vinci’s anatomical drawings, and this took my fiction writing brain back to the end of the middle ages when Da Vinci was alive and ushering the Renaissance in secret labs. 

After writing the fictional letter, I found out that the ossicles themselves were discovered in 1521 by Alessandro Achillini and Jacopo Berengario da Carpi. I did not know this, so I guess I was not too far off the mark with my post-Medieval narrative experiment.

In the letter, I imagined a paranoid world where scientific and technical knowledge that we now take for granted could be received with rumours and superstition. If you're an alchemist or an eager researcher like Leonardo, then next thing you know, when you least expect it, the Inquisition is at your door. As it seems to have happened to anatomists of the time.

I added a plot twist at the end. A mysterious young lady looking for more information on the diagrams. It's a good thing that the assistant had the presence of mind to draw a picture of the enigmatic lady dressed in leather and blue silk. 

<center>![ossicles 2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/litguru/48JeMPK1KTGquT61smXwAhP2JGxMEmsebzv8bf8RQGanFeDqzfuYTdkbxYeHpUP6y2.png)</center>

Thank you for reading.

body.title: I hate Alicante, but it's really not that bad
body.body:
I hate two things in life. Early morning flights is one. Today I had to get up at 0430 to catch my flight to Alicante for the Hive Open Days later this week.
![1000056561.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/Eoc5fGefyuUa66j8HFHVLHh5DLRdn7W7cKknQjWMrMZMvzXfBtFxwkC9kHBpktWJ6vQ.jpg)

The other thing I hate is Alicante . It is infamous in UK for Brits going there for their stag and hen dos. They get wasted for a few days and make a total ass of themselves creating a bad name for Brits abroad. Had it not been for this meet up, Alicante will stay firmly at the bottom of my to go list forever. Alas, Hive had other plans for me.  Still, my hate for Alicante proved me right even before I arrived. 

There was a group of 10-15 guys on my flight on a stag do. They sat in front of me, and boy, were they noisy and deafening. Even the who woman sat behind me shouted at them to shut up. The guys must have bought all the alcohol in board during the two hour flight and were drinking  non stop at 9am in the morning. They were so rowdy and annoying. And to make things worse, the loudest, and most foul mouth guy sat directly in front of me. He even tried to knock down the beer can tower with his miniature bottle of spirit from across the aisle. How can grown up men be so childish and inconsiderate!! I was so glad when we finally got off the plane, my ears were hurting so much 😵‍💫
![1000056566.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EpT3ixy5bex9rr5DjGURGiF6x472XRhyFbFM2ghqSrLVmBxwMJ7atMpriV2XMRY7H2B.jpg)
![livinguktaiwan divider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/fuGLEHxS-livinguktaiwan20divider.png)

After we settled down at the hotel and grabbed some lunch, we went for a walk around town. We stumbled upon the mushroom street. It was fun to see the cute mushroom sculptures and the kids playing there.
<div class=\

> https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EpGQAsJ7HTTL55x3ppvFDPEQcS5wEYDxHx6vucWy4kCbqGAD8FpQDS758FAeyMRgK2D.jpg

I read that Santa Barbara castle offers great views of Alicante and I always enjoy seeing a place from high above. However, I didn't fancy the half hour walk up hill in the heat, and ended up walking around the marina instead. ![1000056593.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/243zZnwK1TuxmKawnHAXJStKBQ4ySb6EQDkzjMMZjV5TJ3JWM3Q4E1ZsyAxMiScWvG1sB.jpg)

> https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EpXHz1xkm6eWq7BXEU4KgtxrYG8LjcZJRczgmU9eCqYGYMA1PQ9ESbd56eWd4LgutzY.jpg --- It was lovely to stroll along the Esplanade. The palm trees offered a nice shade and the mosaic pattern walkway was a very nice touch. ![1000056596.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EogNipSjY4XkLb1GGwMgrpnZQBo1n6TZMVaEFpHQfnr9onLZFFsnXtrPEDeZQb2ym2g.jpg) Suddenly a guy tried to give me a bit of paper. Thinking he was trying to sell me something, I no thanked him. But he was quite insistent and showed me the content. Within a few short seconds, he'd managed to take a photo of us, process and print it. It was actually very impressive. He says it's for me and asked me to keep it. I was happy to do so, don't want my face to end up as rubbish. Now I felt a little bad about it and was wondering if I should leave him a nice comment on his social media. When scanned the QR code, it took me to a restaurant. Ah! Clever advertising. Now I don't feel so bad about it 😄 ![1000056647.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/Ep5o9nkLHCNBqhm9why8fVq1AaA2o8sJbjjwPpgr6SSne7XVbyUZEfTyffnwn8KbEwQ.jpg) --- My last stop of the day was to the neighbourhood of Barrio de Santa Cruz in the old town. It's at the foot of the Santa Barbara castle and involved a little climb. The area is famous for the quaint narrow streets lined with pretty colourful houses. The main one is Las Macetas Azule, The Little House of Blue Pots. There were a few other ones done by up nicely as well.

>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EoGzJhTeVTHZXtc1XBHmYNUcDE9wZSqKjy8FXSsU6DzY2UstkEDqiaP1AR42qykrrH8.jpg https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EpNoNnQrX3iXJNaMGFxcwunExLScKScpJrtnYLeAKQMA9MprsFNDkhYMrvKeVUoDP9n.jpg --- After a long and rather eventful day, I needed to call it a day. I was very happy to see a big bowl of lavender in the hotel lobby when I got back, they smell so nice. Perfect to wind down for the day. Alicante isn't that bad actually, and I think I may like it more when I meet my friends in the next few days. ![1000056640.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/23wgHhJx2iWFAA3K4JCLBcPDKrMoAzaPkNN8ipsQdt9KhbQA3BaUXQ18hzJRsbBoHiqHp.jpg) ![livinguktaiwan divider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/fuGLEHxS-livinguktaiwan20divider.png) ### HPUD Guessing Contest with 200 HP prize Gentle reminder, there's less than 24 hours left to my little contest to celebrate me breaking 200k HP. body.title: Your response is what matters
body.body:
> Change your thoughts and you change your world.

Most of the outcomes we get come from our response to events. We all face the same circumstances—the economy, the government, the weather, the traffic, the road, etc.—but yet get different outcomes at the end of the day. While many complain about everything, a few others have a different response to them and definitely make positive use of every moment as an opportunity. If people get different outcomes from the same event, it shows that the event isn't the actual problem, but the individual response to the event. This only shows how our response shapes the result.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbBe8HrH1tH5NPexDyqzqDquUZZFfWN5Z8tJpCrp1oYAr/1777413087999.png)

**Image generated using Gemini AI**

Change your thoughts and you change your world—this speaks loud. This means the number one person that has hindered your growth or made you produce a bad result isn't the government, economy, or weather, but you. To change anything, which includes your world, all you have to do is change your thoughts. As long as your thought pattern remains the same, nothing changes. You can't do the same thing and expect a different result. If anything has to change, then first you have to change your thoughts and respond differently to events.

We own our world, and it's shaped by our thoughts and responses to events around us. Whatever we are going through or have gone through, there are people who have gone through that phase and come out strong. It isn't about socioeconomic status, strength, or some sort of advantage, but our response to events. Once we change our thoughts, we automatically change what matters in our world.

body.title: [🏖️ENG-🌊ESP] Isla del Rey, a little paradise in Puerto Cabello, Venezuela.
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmV1F93Qjq8XVHSfa4SCZ4kUE7ZbVPxrnW5mysoCZKBDZP/1777391962343.png)

 I remember when I was little, the adults in my family would take my siblings, my cousins, and me to the beach on special occasions. I believe the beautiful and fun memories I have of those getaways are partly why I love everything related to the sea so much—experienced from the shore, of course! I wouldn't dare take up a seafaring life, and I don't even know how to swim 🤣.

​🌊*Recuerdo que cuando era pequeña, los adultos de la familia nos llevaban a mis hermanos, mis primos y a mí a la playa en ocasiones especiales, y creo que los recuerdos bonitos y divertidos que tengo de esas escapadas son en parte lo que hace que me guste tanto todo lo relacionado con el mar; el mar experimentado desde la orilla claro, ¡no me atrevería a lanzarme a la vida marinera, y ni siquiera sé nadar!*🤣

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNMfXozfgfdDxZv8KsAZHBuThAUC7fGwBriSopG99eBcs/1777314284515.jpg)

🏖️ Fortunately, the city of Puerto Cabello is relatively close to where my family lives, which made it possible to make the trip every now and then. If we had been settled in a district far from the coast, deeper into the country's interior, perhaps we wouldn't have known the sea back then—just as there are still so many beautiful tourist spots in Venezuela that we have yet to explore.

​🌊 *Afortunadamente la ciudad de Puerto Cabello queda moderadamente cerca de donde vive mi familia, lo que favorecía poder hacer el viaje de vez en cuando. Si hubiésemos estado asentados en algún Distrito lejano a la costa, más al interior del país, quizás no hubiésemos podido conocer el mar en ese entonces, así como todavía nos faltan por conocer tantos lugares turísticos hermosos de Venezuela.*

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWakA5RgfRzA3x4dNkf4gWHcZskFvbNCdjJiKh7p1hySJ/1777314284626.jpg)

🏖️ This port, being so important to the country, has many beaches, and we still have quite a few left to visit and discover.

​🌊 *Pero este puerto tan importante del país tiene muchas playas, y aún nos quedan unas cuantas por visitar y conocer.*

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXcEmzZt4LjENFg9THkpXJ5K1UBEf5QdYCLzmDSQAu7kF/1777394205173.png)

🏖️ It was so exciting for my husband and me when we agreed last year that we could save some money to go visit our country for the first time in many years since we migrated. The main goal, of course: to spend time with our family and friends.

​🌊 *Fue muy emocionante para mi esposo y para mí cuando acordamos el año pasado que podíamos guardar algo de dinero para ir a visitar nuestro país por primera vez en muchos años desde que migramos. El objetivo principal, por su puesto: compartir con nuestros familiares y amigos.*

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma1WBykWU4ubqekTvQJ7T5Mr62p1kVFQjBDZpB4CKxbzM/1777314284687.jpg)

🏖️ During our month-long stay, the days flew by. Most of the time was spent going from place to place, visiting our families, who don't live very close to each other. We also came down with the flu during the last week. In short, we were having such a good time that the month was ending before we even realized it. But a few days before our return, some of my husband's friends took charge of the plans, picked us up in their car, and took us to Puerto Cabello. We were on our way to contemplate once again some of the landscapes of a place so special in my childhood memories.

​🌊 *Estando allá durante un mes los días se pasaron volando. La mayor parte del tiempo la aprovechamos yendo de un lado a otro, visitando a nuestras familias, que no viven muy cerca una de la otra. También nos enfermamos de una gripe en la última semana. En resumen, lo estábamos pasando tan bien que el mes ya iba a terminar sin que nos diéramos cuenta. Pero unos amigos de mi esposo tomaron las riendas de los planes a pocos días de nuestro regreso, pasaron recogiéndonos en su carro y nos llevaron a Puerto Cabello. Rumbo a contemplar una vez más algunos de los parajes de un lugar tan especial en mis recuerdos de la infancia.*

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWu7e8y9iLU955FYUv3BAr44hBf8f4psYL4jUPeo89Sqq/1777314284768.jpg)

🏖️ This time, however, our friends took us to a spot in the Port we had never been to before: a cluster of beaches within the Naval Base. Access used to be restricted to military use, but it is now open to tourism.

​🌊 *Pero esta vez nuestros amigos nos llevaron a un punto del Puerto en el que nunca habíamos estado, un conjunto de playas dentro de la Base Naval, cuyo acceso solía estar restringido a uso militar y ahora está abierto al turismo.*

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmceBdVbsVeGpLFHiSTMQqTuNWMJ3Ae2WNGQB3ytedhVJy/1777314284812.jpg)

🏖️ Upon entering the base, there is a $5 entrance fee. We were then led to the Playa Delfín pier, where you pay $3 per person for the boat trip to Isla del Rey, which is the closest island to the mainland. I was quite surprised by the prices; honestly, I thought it would be more expensive. Moreover, both the pier beach and the island beach are very well-maintained and clean.

​🌊 *Al entrar a la base hay que pagar una entrada de 5$. Después fuimos conducidos al embarcadero de la Playa Delfín, donde se pagan 3$ por persona por el viaje en lancha desde allí a la Isla del Rey, que es la más cercana a tierra firme. Los precios me sorprendieron bastante, la verdad yo creí que sería más costoso. Además tanto la playa del embarcadero como la de la isla están muy cuidadas y limpias.*

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZUheJmqywsQoPvy3DRXYTe3af8FwffCn2H9zFXNbdPYk/1777314423869.jpg)

🏖️ Additionally, the boat operators were incredibly kind and attentive, helping each passenger embark and disembark and ensuring we all followed the necessary measures for a safe trip.

​🌊 *Además, los operadores de la lancha fueron súper amables y atentos, ayudando a cada pasajero a embarcar y desembarcar, y asegurándose de que todos cumpliéramos con las medidas necesarias para que hiciéramos un viaje seguro.*

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVESjF28BjNQoGMfuyAgG4JiU2Fo1QBJUkk6JdZYBoGvb/1777314423921.jpg)
<sub>*(This is my photo for the contest #aroundtheworld created and runed by @busipuci)*</sub>
[//]:# (!worldmappin 10.49577 lat -67.99164 long Isla del Rey, Puerto Cabello, Venezuela d3scr)


 ​🏖️ Since we arrived quite early, there were no other people besides us and the other family sharing the boat ride. Seeing the crystal-clear water and white sand mixed with golden and pink tones practically empty gave me the feeling of being in a dream, or in paradise. As the day went on, more people arrived, but it was never crowded. Our friends, who go there often, told us it’s always quiet and peaceful. It was almost like being on a private island.

​🌊 *Como llegamos bastante temprano no habían más personas además de nosotros y la otra familia con la que compartimos el trayecto en lancha. Ver prácticamente vacía la playa de agua cristalina y arena blanca mezclada con tonos dorados y rosados me dio la sensación de estar en un sueño, o en el paraíso. Al transcurrir el día llegaron más personas, pero la afluencia no fue demasiada y nuestros amigos, que van allí seguido, nos dijeron que siempre que van hay poca gente y es muy tranquilo. Fue casi como estar en una isla privada.*

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWmpRzh4HSs9GeTQ1vBd8DJhQGXPkHf6RbgfttntxfJz8/1777314423982.jpg)

🏖️ I took this other photo from the boat. I really like it, even though my finger is in the frame, because you can see the bright sunbeam passing through the few clouds in the sky.

​🌊 *Esta otra foto la tomé en la lancha, me gustó mucho aunque aparezca mi dedo, porque se ve el rayo de sol luminoso que pasaba entre las pocas nubes que había.*

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaBJuqHQTPR5hUmfFcnRyLh5zx4bkhRcqo9RHeoKiFG3X/1777314424038.jpg)

🏖️ Apparently, this pink hue in the sand is found on Caribbean beaches surrounded by coral reefs. It is the remains of these reefs and the fossils of small microorganisms living in them that wash up with the waves, tinting the shore with their beautiful color.

​🌊 *Al parecer este color rosado en la arena se ve en las playas caribeñas que están rodeadas de arrecifes de coral y son los restos de estos y los fósiles de los pequeños microorganismos que viven en ellos los que llegan con las olas hasta la playa, tiñendo la orilla con su hermoso color.*

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeAFekL9xbNTZM2KcaVXAA9pnF27uPR4D7CMG4esN5Zq6/1777314703458.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcWYHGWYXk4fYsX1j2Hoag1m8YVnH5f2F5iScPNSMYEpA/1777314506832.jpg)

🏖️ While we were swimming, we saw many little fish under that dock over there. Since I don’t swim, my main entertainment was staying right there in the shallow water, watching those cute creatures.

​🌊 *Cuando nos estábamos bañando vimos muchos pecesitos bajo ese muelle de allí; como yo no nado, fue mi mayor entretenimiento quedarme allí donde el agua es bajita observando a esas lindas criaturas.*

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbZcWQFHHCvE1VKWcAFy149nyk4oUPUZpAUAV9Y2qHQWM/1777314506986.jpg)
 
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZk3TJjo3eYaRy2ceQtn83is1yQrqwc3hWZZ8AH58G6Kr/1777314506929.jpg)

 🏖️ Then another companion arrived—a feathered one this time. When I took this photo, he seemed to be meditating while contemplating the horizon. I took more photos of this model, but I’ll share them in another post; you’ll see how handsome he is 😌.

​🌊 *Luego llegó otro acompañante, esta vez un plumífero, que cuando le tomé esta foto parecía estar meditando mientras contemplaba el horizonte. A este modelo le hice más fotos, pero las compartiré en otro post, ya verán lo guapo que es*😌.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeZQtSBH5Jrm6MgGBhauP3hS3yBYoT5xkAVgaEBWs4f1Z/1777314703386.jpg)

🏖️ Thank you for reading my post and joining me in remembering this adventure that was so special to me 🩵. Below, I’m leaving the link to the contest by @busipuci in case you’d like to participate too! 😁.

​🌊 *Gracias por leer mi post, acompañándome a recordar esta aventura que fue tan especial para mí* 🩵. *A continuación les estaré dejando el link del concurso de @busipuci por si quieren participar también* 😁.

body.title: How do demon exist and how do they multiply? || MCGI topic review
body.body:
Greetings!

https://youtu.be/ILlEsshEbc0?si=1Yuy1lliU3BG0HcT

Are demons truly present in our world? Many people believe they are. According to this belief, demons are spiritual beings that exist beyond what our physical eyes can see. Though invisible, they are thought to be active across the earth. The Bible gives insight into this idea, especially in the book of Job, where Satan tells God that he has been moving to and fro throughout the world. This suggests that Satan and his forces are not confined but operate freely, influencing events and people in unseen ways.

As spiritual beings, demons are believed to affect the physical world even though they remain hidden. While humans cannot see them, it is often said that they can see us. This highlights the belief that the spiritual realm has a strong influence over the physical realm. Many people point to the growing level of wickedness, violence, and moral decline in society as evidence of this unseen activity.

In today’s world, we see a lack of respect for human life, increasing disobedience, and actions driven by selfish or harmful desires. Some attribute these behaviors to negative spiritual influence. Even the rejection of the message of Jesus Christ is, by some, seen as a result of spiritual blindness caused by these forces.

Despite all this, there is hope. Believers are encouraged to remain grounded in the word of God and to live according to His teachings. By doing so, they believe they can resist evil influences and overcome spiritual oppression. Holding firmly to faith is seen as a way to experience freedom, peace, and protection, even in a world where darkness may seem present.

Thanks for reading.

body.title: 28 April 2026, Freewriters Community Daily Writing Prompt Day 3087: patent lie
body.body:
/>  
[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/search/patent%20lie/)

Others see it right away but hesitate, considering the price of speaking up. That moment the lie takes hold by the lack of opposition rather than by strength.

Telling such a lie has an odd audacity. It indicates either ignorance or a profound awareness that many people avoid conflict. And so it rests there, unanswered, increasingly more at ease the longer it remains unused. The longer it stays, the more it starts to define the mood, gently affecting what is accepted and what is overlooked.

A patent lie, however, cannot last forever. Under straightforward examination, it cracks; under undeniable proof, it collapses; it fades when one finally concludes that silence is no more a choice. It only endures where honesty is evasive.

Ultimately, a patent lie is more about bravery, or the lack of it, than it is about deception. It inquires of everyone there quietly: will you allow this stand or will you speak what must be spoken.

body.title: It Might Be Glitch
body.body:
Some people believe in ghosts, I do too because I've encountered something like that before, but others don’t. I’ve watched my share of scary movies and felt that uneasy thrill they bring. There’s always been something distant about those stories though, something that makes them feel safe. You can turn off the screen, walk away, and remind yourself it’s not real but what I felt then when I encountered something I can called a ghost was real.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmUrpBEpjg613DEgvyb9skLoaberFL589ZtAvQuuUEj1ff/1000209322.jpg 

[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/phone-technology-mobile-internet-869669/)
But thinking about a ghost existing in the digital world changes that completely because we spend most of our lives connected to technology now ranging  from social media, Work, conversations, and some of our  memories, everything is stored somewhere online or inside a device. I know people who practically live behind their screens, especially programmers who dedicate endless hours building and maintaining digital systems. One of my friends back is the college was a computer engineer, so imagining him dying suddenly, God forbid and somehow remaining present in that same digital space doesn’t feel as far-fetched as it probably should.

If I were in that situation, I don’t think I would react calmly at first. I had notice small things, files moving, messages appearing, maybe a familiar name showing up online when it shouldn’t. At the beginning, I would try to explain it logically. I’d assume it’s a glitch, a hack, or some kind of software issue. That’s the mindset most of us  would have  there iss always a technical explanation.

But if it continued, I don't want to imagine it to became personal because if the messages reflected memories, conversations, or details only that person would know,then I’d have to face something I couldn’t easily explain. That’s when it would start to feel real, and honestly, that’s when the fear would settle in.

What makes it worse is that there is no clear escape. With a physical place, you can leave. With technology, it follows you. Your phone, your laptop, your accounts, it’s all connected. Shutting one device off wouldn’t feel like enough. There would always be that thought in the back of my mind that it’s still there, waiting the next time I log in.

I don’t see myself panicking completely, but I wouldn’t ignore it either. I’d start pulling away from the digital world as much as I could. Limit my time online, disconnect unnecessary accounts, maybe even switch devices off entirely. At the same time, I’d still try to understand what’s happening. Part of me would want to believe there’s a rational explanation, something grounded in reality.

Even though  it might be the presence of someone I knew, it would be even harder to process. There would be a strange mix of fear and familiarity. I wouldn’t see it as something normal, but I also wouldn’t immediately see it as something evil. It might just be something unresolved, something lingering.

Still, I don’t think I’d ever be comfortable with it. Technology is supposed to be controlled, predictable. Once that boundary is broken, it changes how you see everything. Every notification, every message, every unexpected movement on a screen would carry a different weight.I’d try to distance myself, stay grounded, and hold onto logic as much as possible and maybe  sending myself back to the olden days when there is no technology whatsoever or maybe not. But I know one thing for sure, after something like that, I’d never feel completely alone online again.




**Thank for checking on my blog and have a wonderful day**

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@leemah1/it-might-be-glitch--l1p)

body.title: Digital Ghost
body.body:
DIGITAL GHOST
Tell us what you'll do in such a situation? How'd you escape from a digital ghost? Do you feel fear from the digital ghost, or is this a normal thing for you? What if someday you find a colleague's ghost in your mobile after his death???

Hello #scifimultiverse friends, happy new week. I welcome you to my blog.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR6kRNztoSQxXkE2QV9CTREWYkk5FdXYQkfnmje2Exgdt/1777408410352.jpg)

[Hansuan_Fabregas](https://pixabay.com/images/download/hansuan_fabregas-ghost-7556683_1920.jpg)

A ghost can be defined as someone who died before but came back to continue living. I have heard of these stories before now. Just today, during our office closing hour, one of my colleagues was gisting us about how his grandma’s sister died and relocated to the Northern part of the country of my origin. While there, she was busy sending Onions home through another woman who did not know that she was late. However, the woman was informed that the person she was running errands for was late. She travelled to that same location, and couldn’t find the woman again. Things are happening.


Imagine me in a situation with a digital ghost, huh, someone I’ve known for some time and related to. Capped with some moves, I will say mystic moves since the person is now a ghost. It will be a weird situation in the first instance. But if the person is someone I was cool with when alive. I will be calm after the initial weirdness. But if the situation is horrific, I will try to avoid the digital moves by either changing the system settings or removing the add-ons or anything that generates such moves from the system. I can even go as far as formatting the system because my mental health and peace are paramount.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSr25qSTxcnrDTQhcpGJa4bqsD6AzsLihmgNojUFsUnMN/1777412377009.jpg)
[Shiwa ID](https://unsplash.com/photos/space-gray-iphone-6-on-brown-wooden-table-ZM5dAqCh9AA)

Additionally, the fear may wind down after the first few weeks, while I become calmer and slip back into my normal life with the system. But my challenge with such situations, like finding a colleague's ghost on my phone, will be going to bed and having nightmares about it; otherwise, with time, I will be okay and flow with the digital ghost trend.


Feel free to join [here](https://ecency.com/hive-111030/@scifimultiverse/scifi-multiverse-prompt-week-65-edition-1-or-digital-ghost-or)

body.body:
Hello my friends! I'll be sharing you my dinner today.
This homemade teriyaki chicken breast turned out deliciously glossy and flavorful. The secret lies in two key ingredients:
• Soy sauce: It provides the deep umami base that defines teriyaki, balancing saltiness with richness.
• Cornstarch (maicena): Essential for thickening the sauce, giving it that silky texture that clings perfectly to the chicken.
I didn’t have sesame seeds this time, but the chopped green onions added a fresh crunch and color contrast. Even without sesame, the dish was satisfying and full of flavor.

Hola amigos! Les estaré compartiendo mi comida de hoy.
Esta pechuga de pollo teriyaki casera quedó brillante y llena de sabor. El secreto está en dos ingredientes clave:
• Salsa de soya: Aporta la base umami profunda que define el teriyaki, equilibrando la sal con riqueza.
• Maicena: Fundamental para espesar la salsa y darle esa textura sedosa que se adhiere perfectamente al pollo.
En esta ocasión no tenía semillas de sésamo, pero la cebollita verde picada aportó frescura y contraste de color. Aunque sin sésamo, el plato resultó muy sabroso y completo.

body.title: The quiet time || my greatest time
body.body:
Greetings!

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTEo77xivPU23QaaHbCEHkPTmbFeworRa2MYpn2U5deUA/img_1719838251519.jpg)

One of those times I love so much as a person is my quite time which is used to be devoid of distraction and noise pollution. 

The quiet time is that part of my life that helps me to self discover myself. This particular said time has always been my greatest asset which has helped to transform me from my low estate to the high estate of my life.

Having said this, I would like to delve into the topic of the prompt which is all about “a quiet time.” 

To me, a quiet time is a time that is devoid of distraction and pollution and if there's a time that we must all crave for as humans and as an individual, then the time must be the quiet and this is not because of any other thing, but because of what is embedded in the quiet time.

In the quiet time, there are numerous good things embedded in it. One of those thing is seriousness. In the quiet time, there's this level of seriousness that comes to everyone and this is because the quiet time is always devoid of distraction and noise pollution. 

This level of seriousness has overtime for me transformed into self discovery. Through the quiet time, I have been able to discover both my weakness and strength in life. 

So, for this reason, I know what I'm capable of doing and at the same time, what I'm not capable of doing. I wouldn't have known this if not for the existence of quiet as I would have played my life away.

But for the quiet time, I have been able to have this self retreat and not only that, I have also been able to think deep of my past, present and the future and as a result of this, I have been able to do the right thing which has really helped in shaping my life.

I could remember the last time I had this kind of a personal retreat. Then, things were not going as expected for me and as a result, I talked to a friend named Oluseun. It's this friend of mine that advised me to have a quiet time of mine and think deeply about my past, present and future. 

I did as this friend of mine told me and that's when I got to know the power of quiet time as the end result was a success.

Also, there's this aura or spirit with the quiet time that transforms the life of people who observe it and that spirit really worked with me and now, I'm now a living testimony of what a quiet time can be and do. 

The quiet time has always been my abode and strength to achieve great things in life and anytime I need fresh strength and energy,  most especially when I'm down, I turn to the quiet time and the end result has always been a success story to me and that I would always do as the impact of this in my life can never be overemphasized. 

This is my entry to the week 215, episode 01 of the weekly Featured contest in the Hive Learners community. 

Thanks for reading.

links.title: THE IMPORTANCE OF quiet time
links.body: > ![THE IMPORTANCE OF quiet time.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rimurutempest/23vsSynQpAHgMs5VVyKifYccjdNSTenjk4spFnLFqVYnEoPSZqpdSbVk6y9Ea3hPjMnxR.jpg) We live in a globalized world, which means we are connected to the whole world and to everyone, all at the same time. Confusing? No, that's the power of globalization. In the past, people were restricted to their neighborhood, their city, and at most – generally – their country. However, with the advancement of communication and transportation technologies, access to culture and products from other countries is much easier and more accessible. But doesn't this great ease have a negative side? I remember a love story that says it's much harder to find someone today because the bar has been raised with globalization. Does that make sense? Just as access to culture and news has become global, so have romantic possibilities. With the implementation of dating apps and social networks increasing interaction with people far away, your universe of possibilities expands and the demands increase. This is one example that shows how the advancement of globalization has impacted people's lives, increasing anxiety because they begin to compare themselves to others who are distant from their reality, who haven't experienced the same issues, and who are possibly only selecting the best moments of their lives and day to post online. Like the equivalent exchange in the anime Fullmetal Alchemist, in life there is always a tendency towards balance; if there has been great progress, problems related to it have certainly arisen. With more access, people begin to consume content and news that won't change their lives in any way, wasting their time. Boredom has disappeared because today you can access streaming services, social media, games, and everything else with the current level of technology. And you know what you don't have? TIME! Time for calm, tranquility, so you can think about life and rethink your choices. I'll be much appreaciated if you **Votes**, **Reblogs** or give any **Tips**. Thanks and have good reading! 🍀 ---

>

## The Importance of Quiet Time!

<center> https://img.leopedia.io/DQmfZ5VSX5YQ2F94WNqYYKBmfVRS5TBCEev8CCZF7UZyHpc/image.png </center>
<center>[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/)</center>

Sometimes I find myself in a situation where, if I just thought for a little longer, I believe it would be resolved, but because I need to use that time for another task, I end up without enough time for that moment of reflection. That's why I can't quickly recall the last time I calmly stopped to think. However, I am aware that this is extremely important, but at the same time risky, because it can end up interfering with other activities.

The reason is simple. Because modern life is a rush, with information arriving from everywhere, we don't have quiet time to think about things. So, when we decide to stop for a moment to think about the situation we're in, because we've been without this pause for so long, one thing starts piling up after another, and if you stop to think and solve problems, you end up delaying \

tasks that you'll later have to catch up on. It's really difficult, but important. The answer, as usual, is to seek a possible balance, perhaps by allocating a moment every X amount of time to have this period and to avoid the madness of losing control in the middle of the calm, practicing a little meditation and setting limits regarding time and topics that should be respected, so that it doesn't disrupt the rest of your life, and on the contrary, serves as a moment to reaffirm decisions and recalculate your course. --- https://img.leopedia.io/DQmeCJZEK6UG5Tc3avBibmLNHkgkN9PXcmVN1jYhHR6aHGG/image.png ---

> ![THE IMPORTANCE OF quiet time.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rimurutempest/23vsSynQpAHgMs5VVyKifYccjdNSTenjk4spFnLFqVYnEoPSZqpdSbVk6y9Ea3hPjMnxR.jpg) Vivemos em um mundo globalizado, o que significa que estamos conectados ao mundo todo e à todo mundo, tudo ao mesmo tempo. Confuso? Não, esse é o poder da globalização. Antigamente, as pessoas estavam restritas ao seu bairro, sua cidade e no máximo - no geral - ao seu país. Entretanto, com o avanço das tecnologias de comunicação e dos transportes, o acesso à cultura e aos produtos de outros países está muito mais fácil e acessível. Mas será que essa grande facilidade não tem um lado negativo? Lembro de uma história de amor, que diz que hoje está muito mais difícil de encontrar alguém, porque a régua aumentou com a globalização. Será que faz sentido? Do mesmo jeito que o acesso à cultura e notícias agora virou global, as possibilidades amorosas também estão. Com a implementação de aplicativos de namoro e de redes sociais aumentando a interação com pessoas longe de você, o seu universo de possibilidades expande e as exigências aumentam. Esse é um dos exemplos que mostram como o avanço da globalização impactou na vida das pessoas aumentando a ansiedade, porque elas começam a se comparar um outra que está distante da realidade dela, que não passou pelas mesmas questões e possivelmente está selecionando apenas os melhores momentos da vida e do dia para postar na Internet. Como na troca equivalente do anime Fullmetal Alchemist, na vida existe sempre tendemos a um equilíbrio, se houve uma grande progresso certamente surgiram problemas relacionados à ele. Com mais acesso, as pessoas começam a consumidor conteúdos e notícias que não vão mudar em nada a vida delas, gastando sem tempo. O tédio sumiu, porque hoje você pode acessar streamings, redes sociais, jogos e tudo mais com o nível de tecnologia atual. E sabe o que você não tem? TEMPO! Um tempo de calma, tranquilidade, para que você possa pensar na vida e repensar as escolhas. Fico agradecido se você puder dar um **Voto**, **Reblogs** ou algum **Tips**. Obrigado e boa leitura! 🍀 ---

>

## A Importância do Tempo Calmo!

<center> https://img.leopedia.io/DQmfZ5VSX5YQ2F94WNqYYKBmfVRS5TBCEev8CCZF7UZyHpc/image.png </center>
<center>[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/)</center>

As vezes eu me encontra uma situação em que se eu apenas pensasse por um pouco mais de tempo eu acredito que elas seria resolvida, mas pela necessidade de utilizar o tempo para uma outra tarefa, acabo ficando sem um excesso de tempo para ter justamente esse momento de reflexão. Por isso, que não me recordo rapidamente da última vez que parei com calma para pensar. Entretanto, tenho consciência de que isso é extremamente importante, mas ao mesmo tempo arriscado, porque pode acabar atrapalhando as suas outras atividades.

O motivo é simples. Como a vida moderna é uma correria, com informações chegando por todos os lugares, não temos tempo calmo para pensar nas coisas. Assim, quando resolvemos parar um pouco para pensar no cenário em que estamos, por estarmos tanto tempo sem essa pausa, começa a vir uma coisa atrás da outra e com isso se você para para pensar e resolver, você vai atrasando as tarefas \

e que depois vai ter que correr atrás. É realmente difícil, mas importante. A resposta, como de costume, é buscar um possível equilíbrio, talvez pensando em alocar um momento a cada X tempo para ter esse período e para evitar essa loucura de perder o controle no meio da calma, praticar um pouco de meditação e se import limites com relação à tempo e tópicos que devem ser respeitados, para que não atrapalhe o restante da vida, e pelo contrário, sirva de um momento que vai reafirmar as decisões e recalcular a rota. ---

>***Don't  stop till you serve kings.....***


currently  I'm working for a lady, a cake artist a very very exceptionally good one at that, it's  not long I started working with her but from what Info I have gathered this lady is really ontop of the cake  food chain here...

she's  so  good and well connected  she handles  cake for the elites of the society, including  the governor, wife of chieftains,  senators, she has  very wealthy clientele.

one would easily dismissed this as based on who knows who to handle such contracts, but pause this isn't none of those, when I say she worked her ass off to where she is now, I mean it, she is so good that you can just be staring at her cake works and not what to touch it, the best of it's  kind that I've  ever known

excellence raises the bar, if you can attain it you will receive  the crown, any body can get up and do something  but an expert does it with a touch of excellence,  paying keen attention  to details  and making sure that every aspect is strictly  adhered to, excellence is that ability to do a thing exceptionally well that it's  outstanding. 


meanwhile it's  what every body wants, they desire  it but they are not willing  to pay the price, forfiet  immediate  gratification for the greater good


let me ask you, have you ever seen a rolls Royce?, have you entered one before?,  neither do I but the fact is till today rollroyce cars are considered  true   epitome of  excellence, class elegance and  price, mare looking at it you know this cost money, that's  what Excellence  is, a lot of us desires it, but we run away from paying the price and responsibility  that comes with it 

a man once told me, you see this life, at some point whether  you're  born rich or poor you must  pay a price for something  you need, sometimes  it's  beyond  monetary  value,  these prices are the sacrifice  you must  make for the greater good,  

the sad reality is you really can't  eat your cake and have it,  however most people  till today are struggling  to defy the odds...


excellence  will demand diligent,  consistency,  hardwork,  resilience,  steadfastness dogged attitude, paying keen attention  to details, creative mindset,  out of this world imagination , when others says know what do you say..

the picture  above is that of  a cake we were working  on it took us over 2-3hours to finish it, by the time were  done, she came in examined it and flagged it down undo everything  and start all over again, it  hurts really bad but that is the price of excellence,  it's  either the best or nothing, I always tell my self there is no room for mediocrity,  if there is the better version of anything  I always ask myself why can't  I have that one instead,  I can't  settle for less

the prize of excellence  is where she has risen to today, having to  talk and negotiate with high ranking clients  all over the country,  you can't  see her works and not gaze at it for  a minute,...

the prize of excellence  is heavy compared to the price (sacrifices)   you must pay  now if you really want to serve kings.....

links.title: The Book has arrived! The journey has officially begun!
links.body:
Troublemakers! We can't believe it, our very first book has finally arrived. This is something we've been dreaming of doing for years, and today it became a reality.


![IMG_2736.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/thetroublenotes/23yJGamWqUZUq5fNUzMNHW3Pe5YsdBVq3AGyhFfkv11e4Mvn8aR7w9dVyJDnKAqSuWUC6.jpeg)


\

is the Prologue to a massive fictional story album that we've written. It is the most daring project we've ever produced. We took A LOT of risks with this album/story. In a world where AI is becoming more invasive in our lives, this story is intended to be authentic. Most importantly, it's the prototype for a much larger story and project. We are so proud to have had a huge team of people working on this with us. Guest artists from incredible bands who have had fabulous careers. It is illustrated by HUMAN hands and produced by human ears. It's narrative. Dark. Uplifting. And different. There are vocals on some of the songs. There are deep and immersive narrations. And by the end we are hopeful you will be singing with us and following this story, wanting to know more!

We have spent a lot of time behind the scenes preparing for this moment. We debuted some of the new music in Arenas last weekend infront of THOUSANDS of people. They sang with us. They danced with us. The feedback was immense.

So! Get ready because over the next weeks we have so much to share with you. The pre-orders are already rolling in and we will begin playing this music live at our shows. Most importantly, watch this space because we're going to be bringing you deep into the recording and song-writing process of how this came to fruition and where it is going from here. The entire album is just a taste of what's to come!

Love,

TTN HQ

links.title: La música que heredé sin darme cuenta | [ESP/ENG]
links.body:
*Hola a todos, soy nueva en la comunidad y quise empezar escribiendo mi primer post hablando sobre este tema. Mi nombre es Wara y soy de Bolivia, me gusta una gran variedad de géneros musicales, de niña solía tocar el piano y otros instrumentos autóctonos de mi país. Un gusto conocerlos a todos.*

---
¿Te has puesto a pensar que la mayoría de tus gustos musicales vienen de diferentes entornos con los que te relacionas?

![9.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/waralotito/Eoc69fGasgBCPm6paBVDzXiDTCaJ4fgCyEAPz6UTEz36g5z5dW2abNPj9DTAJ327VB6.png)
*(Imagen creada en Canva).*

Me pasó lo mismo hace un tiempo, pero es muy interesante cómo funciona esta dinámica. En mi caso me gustan diferentes géneros de música, pop, rock, electrónica, kpop, salsa y más.

Desde muy pequeña en mi familia siempre estuvo presente la música, ya sea a través de instrumentos musicales, CDs, DVDs y otros medios. También porque parte de mi familia era docente de música.

Empecemos con mi mamá, ella también tenía un gusto muy variado, como el rock, pop, música nacional de Bolivia, música clásica, baladas y similares. En cambio, mi papá prefería el rock en español y especialmente argentino.

También estaban mis abuelos a los que les gustaban los boleros, música nacional, rancheras y los clásicos cantantes mexicanos de antes. Y por último mis tíos y mi prima, escuchaban cosas similares a mi mamá y mis abuelos.

Como pueden ver era una gran variedad de géneros que se escuchaban en mi casa y la verdad había muy pocas canciones que no me gustaban, pero en general los géneros sí me gustaban.

![10.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/waralotito/Ep3gCq2ZxdZSUAQmDA1pE1XFeag6Exw6tD1dn9S9m3FMYAuQ9tsA1SYYivRAWKRgUuv.png)
Mis primeros profes de música, mi tío y mi prima. *(Fotografía de archivo familiar, edición propia en Canva).*

En un principio les había comentado que me puse a pensar cómo cada persona desarrolla o va formando sus propios gustos en cuanto a música, obviamente aplica con otros gustos, pero el entorno influye mucho en estos aspectos.

Creo que tuve suerte al tener papás que escucharan canciones con letras tan bonitas, y no como ahora que son más repetitivas y estridentes, para mi gusto, quizá solo para bailar en una fiesta.

Además, que desde pequeña empecé a tocar el piano, mi primer profesor fue mi propio tío, quien me fue enseñando canciones básicas como feliz cumpleaños, el himno a la alegría y así. A él le gustaba tocar piano, acordeón y cantaba muy bien; si bien era muy estricto, sus estudiantes lo querían mucho.

Luego me pusieron en clases de piano en el colegio y fuera de este, fue más idea de mi mamá que de mi papá jeje. Aquí ya me enseñaron un poco más técnico y profesional todo lo relacionado con la música y el piano, y me hacían tocar canciones más clásicas como Para Elisa, El Animador, entre muchos otros.

Si bien en ese entonces no me gustaba del todo esa música, porque la consideraba difícil y algo aburrida, tuve la oportunidad de tocar algunas canciones que me gustaban como aquellas que eran de las películas de Disney, ya que un profesor del colegio había conseguido todo un libro con sus partituras.

![11.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/waralotito/Ep3gmuKd9J9XGKXLQcZyRbmKpUiR9vXrBEJbvqvQLt4YJuwKr96enV7CkpHtVBALf4N.png)
En algunos conciertos de música. *(Fotografía de archivo familiar, edición propia en Canva).*

Ahora creo que a través de todo lo que viví fue que desarrollé en gran medida mi oído musical, porque logré desarrollar la capacidad de escuchar y diferenciar varias cosas que quizá no todos perciben, por ejemplo, cuando alguien abre la cerradura de la puerta, cuando se acerca algún desfile o el vibrar de un celular.

Parecerá simple, pero a veces suele ser de mucha utilidad y obviamente que sirve bastante en la música. Ahora ya no estoy practicando nada de música, pero me di cuenta de que también tengo buen ritmo, es decir, para bailar, entonces es algo que también me gusta hacer.

Me siento feliz de tener gustos tan variados porque así nunca me aburro de eso jeje además que mi círculo ha crecido mucho más y también me ha influenciado a escuchar más tipos de música.

Es muy interesante cómo funciona todo esto y las influencias que podemos tomar de distintas personas, ya sea para bien o para mal, somos como la suma de varias personas y creo que eso lo hace divertido y hasta multicultural.

Hoy quise hablar sobre este tema, quizá no para dar una reflexión sesuda jeje pero sí para dejarles esa chispita y que se pongan a pensar de dónde provienen sus gustos musicales, quizá de alguna experiencia bonita de niños, jóvenes o adultos pero que lo recuerden.

![12.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/waralotito/Ep5nH1bDmWkVwVvnhKA5K4vwW9zA3v6VzsJrtTJs3BJFH6Ud7JVvaPyxcfL3a8EyyYT.png)
Mis influencias musicales familiares. *(Imagen creada con Chatgpt y editada en Canva).*

También para ver sus raíces, del país y lugar de donde nacieron o se criaron, como también su familia o de su círculo cercano. Como les decía, somos la suma de todo eso, cultura, experiencias, personas, lugares, saberes y más.

¿Y de dónde provienen tus gustos musicales? Cuéntame en los comentarios.

Que tengas una bonita semana.

<details>
<summary> Read in English</summary>

# The Music I Inherited Without Realizing It

*Hi everyone, I’m new to the community and wanted to kick things off by writing my first post on this topic. My name is Wara and I’m from Bolivia; I enjoy a wide variety of musical genres. As a child, I used to play the piano and other traditional instruments from my country. It’s a pleasure to meet you all.*

---
Have you ever stopped to think that most of your musical tastes come from the different environments you’re exposed to?

The same thing happened to me a while back, but it’s really interesting how this dynamic works. In my case, I like different genres of music—pop, rock, electronic, K-pop, salsa, and more.

Music has always been a part of my family since I was very young, whether through musical instruments, CDs, DVDs, or other media. This was also because some of my family members were music teachers.

Let’s start with my mom—she also had very diverse tastes, including rock, pop, Bolivian folk music, classical music, ballads, and similar genres. My dad, on the other hand, preferred rock in Spanish, especially Argentine rock.

Then there were my grandparents, who liked boleros, traditional Bolivian music, rancheras, and classic Mexican singers from the past. And finally, my uncles, aunts, and cousin listened to similar things to my mom and grandparents.

As you can see, there was a wide variety of genres played in my house, and honestly, there were very few songs I didn’t like—but overall, I did enjoy the genres.

At first, I mentioned that I started thinking about how each person develops or forms their own musical tastes—obviously, this applies to other preferences as well—but the environment has a huge influence on these aspects.

I think I was lucky to have parents who listened to songs with such beautiful lyrics, unlike today’s songs, which are more repetitive and loud—at least to my taste—and perhaps only good for dancing at a party.

Also, I started playing the piano when I was little. My first teacher was my own uncle, who taught me basic songs like “Happy Birthday,” “Ode to Joy,” and so on. He liked to play the piano and accordion, and he sang very well; even though he was very strict, his students loved him dearly.

Later, I was enrolled in piano lessons at school and outside of school—it was more my mom’s idea than my dad’s, haha. There, they taught me everything related to music and the piano in a more technical and professional way, and they had me play more classical songs like “Für Elise” and “The Entertainer,” among many others.

Although I didn’t really like that music back then—because I found it difficult and a bit boring—I had the chance to play some songs I did like, such as those from Disney movies, since a teacher at school had gotten his hands on a whole book of sheet music for them.

Now I think that through everything I’ve been through, I’ve really developed my musical ear, because I’ve managed to develop the ability to hear and distinguish various things that perhaps not everyone notices—for example, when someone turns a doorknob, when a parade is approaching, or the vibration of a cell phone.

It might seem simple, but sometimes it’s really useful, and obviously it helps a lot with music. I’m not practicing music at all right now, but I realized I also have a good sense of rhythm—like for dancing—so that’s something I enjoy doing too.

I’m happy to have such varied tastes because that way I never get bored of it, haha, plus my circle has grown a lot and has also influenced me to listen to more types of music.

It’s really interesting how all this works and the influences we can pick up from different people—whether for better or worse—we’re like the sum of various people, and I think that makes it fun and even multicultural.

Today I wanted to talk about this topic, maybe not to offer some deep reflection, haha, but to spark that little thought in you and get you thinking about where your musical tastes come from—maybe from some beautiful experience from when you were a child, a teenager, or an adult, but one that you remember.

Also to look at your roots—the country and place where you were born or raised, as well as your family or close circle. As I was saying, we are the sum of all that: culture, experiences, people, places, knowledge, and more.

Where do your musical tastes come from? Let me know in the comments.

Have a great week.

*(Translated with DeepL)*

links.body:
>Expansiva semana llena de salud, energía, ideas maravillosas, magia. Encuentros con tu propio ser y mucho entusiasmo en cada actividad que realicen.

\n\n

>Esta vez en mis recorridos, como expresé hace unos días más observadora con la naturaleza que me rodea a pesar que no son espacios nuevos para mí. Este pequeño boulevard tiene especies maravillosas, quien sabe si los que caminan por allí todos los días como yo se sorprenden al ver como capturo plantas que allí se encuentran, quien sabe qué preguntas florecen en sus pensamientos, porque son plantas que vemos en diferentes zonas pero sin dar importancia. Como suele decirse, están allí, nos limpian el aire, nos dan sombra, belleza y ya.

>Esta planta que hoy comparto en esta comunidad si es Trinitaria, pero una Trinitaria diferente en el tamaño de sus hojas y la forma como florece, su tronco, no es como la que acostumbramos ver espacios como casas, plazas y otros. Para mí, me atrevo a decir es el único sitio donde la he visto.

\n\n

>En la investigación realizada su nombre científico o latino es Bougainvillea spp. Además, se conoce con diferentes nombres y de acuerdo a la información en diferentes espacios estos nombres son : Buganvilla, Bugambilia, Bugambilias, Santa Rita, Veranera, Trinitaria, Veraneras, Flor de papel, Enredadera de papel, Buganvilia, Buganvil, Santarrita, Camelina.

>Es de la familia: Nyctaginaceae (Nictagináceas). De origen Brasileño. El nombre del género está dedicado al navegante francés Louis de Bougainville.

\n\n

>Así mismo se encuentran varias especies de Buganvillas, híbridos y cultivares (variedades). Las especies más cultivadas son:- Bougainvillea glabra,- Bougainvillea spectabilis,- Arbusto trepador, perennifolio y espinoso. Sus ramas son muy vigorosas y pueden alcanzar hasta 8 metros.

\n\n

>La especie que presento por la forma de sus flores o como florece este árbol se puede concluir que es Bougainvillea glabra. Es nativa de las regiones amazónicas de Colombia, Perú, Brasil, Paraguay y Argentina.

>Esta especie de Trinitaria o Bougainvillea glabra fue descrita por Jacques Denis Choisy y publicada en Prodromus Systematis Naturalis Regni Vegetabilis, en el año 1849.

\n\n
>Jacques Denis Choisy, también conocido como Jacques Denys Choisy o Jacques-Denis Choisy fue un profesor de filosofía, micólogo y botánico suizo.

>Sus flores son muy pequeñas, blancas, fucsia, en grupos con brácteas coloridas papilosas. Se dispone de variedades de sola o doble flor. El tronco leñoso tiende a enroscarse, y las delgadas ramas tienen afiladas espinas y hojas verde oscuras. Es muy buena para setos, arcos, o arbusto en la tierra, y en macetas. Es ideal para bonsái.

\n\n

>Las buganvillas no requieren de sustratos especialmente ricos ni exóticos, sino más bien lo contrario, arraigan en terrenos arcillosos y calcáreos. Pueden florecer durante todo el año aun con heladas, pero alcanzan su máximo esplendor en los meses más cálidos del año. Como esta zona es calurosa, de mucho sol intenso esta planta siempre está florecida, así como aparecen las imágenes.

>Se dice que la infusión de las hojas tiernas y brácteas se utiliza oralmente para el tratamiento de afecciones gastrointestinales (diarrea, dolor de estómago) y respiratorias (asma, bronquitis, catarro, dolor de pecho, fiebre, gripe, pulmonía, ronquera, tos y tos ferina). La decocción de las raíces se usa para tratar fiebres y por su efecto purgante. En realidad, nunca había escuchado sobre esta propiedad de esta planta, siempre considero que la medicina natural es muy amplia, rica y fascinante, a la hora de tomar este tipo de plantas para alguna afección debe ser guiado por un profesional de este tipo de medicina para hacer la indicación correcta, para no alterar y sea fluida la sanación de la persona que la ingiera.

\n\n
>Una planta que su tronco lo considero una obra de arte natural, la forma como está entrelazado, al así como enviando un mensaje, su fortaleza y resistencia es admirable.

>

>May this week be filled with health, energy, wonderful ideas, and magic. May it be a week of encounters with your inner self and great enthusiasm in every activity you undertake.

\n\n

>This time, on my walks, as I mentioned a few days ago, I'm being more observant of the nature that surrounds me, even though these aren't new places for me. This little boulevard has wonderful species. Who knows if those who walk there every day, like me, are surprised to see me photographing the plants I find there? Who knows what questions bloom in their minds? Because these are plants we see in different areas but without giving them much thought. As they say, they're there, they clean the air, they give us shade, beauty, and that's it.

\n\n

>This plant that I'm sharing with this community today is indeed a bougainvillea, but a different kind of bougainvillea in the size of its leaves and the way it blooms. Its trunk isn't like the ones we're used to seeing in places like houses, plazas, and other locations. For me, I dare say, it's the only place I've seen it.

\n\n

>In this research, its scientific or Latin name is Bougainvillea spp. It is also known by various other names, including: Buganvilla, Bugambilia, Bugambilias, Santa Rita, Veranera, Trinitaria, Veraneras, Flor de papel, Enredadera de papel, Buganvilia, Buganvil, Santarrita, and Camelina.

\n\n

>It belongs to the Nyctaginaceae family and is native to Brazil. The genus name is dedicated to the French navigator Louis de Bougainville.

There are several species of Bougainvillea, as well as hybrids and cultivars (varieties). The most commonly cultivated species are: Bougainvillea glabra and Bougainvillea spectabilis. It is a climbing, evergreen, and thorny shrub with vigorous branches that can reach up to 8 meters in length.

>The species I am presenting, based on the shape of its flowers and how this tree blooms, can be identified as Bougainvillea glabra. It is native to the Amazonian regions of Colombia, Peru, Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina.

\n\n

>This species of Trinitaria, or Bougainvillea glabra, was described by Jacques Denis Choisy and published in Prodromus Systematis Naturalis Regni Vegetabilis in 1849.

\n\n

>Jacques Denis Choisy, also known as Jacques Denys Choisy or Jacques-Denis Choisy, was a Swiss professor of philosophy, mycologist, and botanist.

\n\n

>Its flowers are very small, white or fuchsia, in clusters with colorful, papillose bracts. Single-flowered and double-flowered varieties are available. The woody trunk tends to twine, and the slender branches have sharp thorns and dark green leaves. It is very good for hedges, arches, or as a shrub in the ground and in pots. It is ideal for bonsai. Bougainvilleas don't require particularly rich or exotic soils; quite the opposite, they thrive in clay and calcareous soils. They can bloom year-round, even in frosts, but reach their peak during the warmer months. Since this area is hot and sunny, this plant is always in bloom, as you can see in the pictures.

\n\n

>It is said that an infusion of the tender leaves and bracts is used orally to treat gastrointestinal ailments (diarrhea, stomach ache) and respiratory conditions (asthma, bronchitis, catarrh, chest pain, fever, flu, pneumonia, hoarseness, cough, and whooping cough). A decoction of the roots is used to treat fevers and for its purgative effect. Actually, I had never heard of this property of this plant before. I always consider natural medicine to be very broad, rich, and fascinating. When taking these types of plants for any ailment, it should be guided by a qualified practitioner to ensure the correct prescription and to avoid disrupting the healing process for the person taking it.

\n\n

>I consider the trunk of this plant a work of natural art; the way it's intertwined, as if conveying a message, its strength and resilience are admirable.

links.title: MCGI Topic Review | Depression and anxiety, how to overcome these biblically
links.body: > https://youtu.be/mtz3NLb9KXw?si=JH1t_Ri386mbvrPE If there is a popular issue that a whole lot of people are presently facing in the world and society right now, it is the depression and Anxiety issue. It is really becoming a major real struggle that a whole lot of people even me sometimes have faced. There are actually moments that my hearts have really been so heavy. My thoughts have really been so restless and I don't really have strength to vene keep going. But one of the things that have keep me going is the fact that the bible keeps teaching us that we are not alone. God actually see our pain and he actually cares so much for us. In the book of Psalm 34:18, the Bible says, “The Lord is close to the brokenhearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit. There is actually a comfort that I have been able to feel that always reminds me that no matter what I am facing or passing through, God is near. I may not actually feel his presence but one of the things that I can never deny is the fact that His word always assured me that there is hope for me and not only that but the fact that he is actually holding me. If there is actually one way I have been able to overcome anxiety, I will say it is through prayer. I don't joke with prayers. Whenever my mind is actually full of worries, I make sure that I talked to God. I make sure that I tell him everything. In Philippians 4:6-7, it says, “Do not be anxious about anything, but in every situation, by prayer and petition… present your requests to God.” When I do this, I feel a kind of peace that I cannot explain. It calms my heart little by little.

links.title: The Kind of Friend Everyone Prays For
links.body:
School days at the university gave me a lot of friends that are amazing and those I hold dear to my heart to this day. Although not all of these friendships began on a smooth path, some began through a fight, misunderstanding, disappointment, and the like, but we were able to put our differences aside and create awesome memories through the years. It's been over ten years since I graduated from the university, and I'm still best of friends with many of these people, some of whom are my course mates, roommate, fellow friends, and the like. But today I want to talk about a friend I made at my place of worship during my undergraduate days and how good of a friend she was. ![1000769404.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vickoly/2466rh5tB4sf4QZboesy4epQbi4xKahvkyMbwJSKGB3vtpHeLSShX7aaoqn3NgMf4FWj1.jpg) The first time we met was at a church service when she first came to inform the head usher of my church that she'd love to join the ushering department; it was during a special program in the evening, and I remember she happened to be a free and outspoken person who isn't shy in new places or around new people like I am. So we kinda hit it off immediately to become friends; after the service, we, alongside my friends, walked together till she got to her house avenue, and we departed. The following day was my first time seeing her in the school compound, and I got to know she was a fresher while I was in my third year. The bond of the friendship grew more thanks to the fact that we were both in the ushering department in the church, and we kind of encouraged each other to be more active and fervent in the house of God. This was so because most other people in the ushering department were mostly adults who I could hardly relate with due to the age gap. Additionally, being a fresher, I've a lot of ways of helping her with her academics, be it in studying or providing her with some of my previous course handbooks. Also, she happens to be a generous individual who gives freely; for instance, on most occasions when we've had church services like vigil, she'll bring an extra meal for me when coming to church with hers. Being a young man from a not-too-rich home, I'm always grateful for her generosity. I can even remember she once gave me her second phone when I misplaced my phone during my undergraduate days. Aside from the academic assistance I rendered to her, it's more or less like she's the one doing most of the giving. But thankfully I could compensate for that by giving her an opportunity to learn freely in her profession she's passionate about, which is catering, event decoration, and the like, and that's because I work as a staffing agent for most of the caterers and event decorators in our school vicinity, so I usually let her tag along to broaden her knowledge, and now she's into that profession herself. Although many of my friends do think we're dating, we've never dated, nor have I had such feelings towards her; to me, she's more like a friend and a younger sister. And till this day we're still friends. I'm married to the love of my life, and so is she, and we both are still friends; in fact, we both still attend the same church and both still work as ushers in the church. I'm thankful for the gift of her because she's a friend indeed. *** All photos are mine. ***
Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@vickoly/the-kind-of-friend-everyone-prays-for-efk)

links.title: Highlighting Selection Bias
links.body:
>

I have liked playing around with some photos lately to make them look more like prints or posters - limited colour range, flattened, lots of saturation. relatively simple pictures with a bit of detail, that gets lost in the flattening. I don't know if they are good or not for your eyes, but I like them. 

---


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/23xytiTCDGy8EgYoFFgwHibq6zj37JnDjF21kqkamx2fJZTCsQ8MAUFb9oKU8p5xEUyCX.png)


---

There is nothing overly difficult about doing this in Lightroom (mobile), but I think that it makes what would otherwise be a useless image, usable. And lately I have been looking for interesting images to work with and even if they are low-quality, they can come up pretty well.

The original of the image above:

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/23tc9u3AMQYrQNfQ3xYaUCZxoLjHrimmvqBvagV5zDbdYpRxmppMLqQsoLG419AY7xrfS.png)

As said, not a great image, or quality of image, as it was taken on 10x zoom on my mobile from a long way away from the lighting. With a little bit of work though, and it is good enough (in my books) for an article image to support the topic, which is going to watch my daughter sing with her class at a Mother's Day concert. 

She is at one of the schools that has more music support, and the association that covers them and raises money for various activities collects them all together occasionally for a concert, with the Mother's Day one being the main event. And before you ask, there is not even a minor Father's Day concert - there is nothing - *as usual.* 

But Smallsteps was super excited about taking part in her first proper concert like this and has been practicing at home and with the class, and then with a rehearsal onsite today during class hours. After the concert, her aunty and grandparents also came to see her, she was asking about our favourite bits and what she liked and what it was like backstage. 

> I would put a photo but there are far too many other children in the pictures, so it would all just be blur.

The concert was good, with each school singing a couple songs in a theme. Smallsteps' school sang songs from *The Sound of Music,* which is why we watched it the other weekend so she could have more connection to what she was singing about. It helped a lot and I also think that she enjoyed the movie more, because she could \

while watching. Anyway, I have been to several school concerts and dance events over the last few years, and what was evident at this one was how strong the selection bias is with these kids. At other events there is always a wide range of children who are on a spectrum of both skill and interest, including those who don't care at all and run around like the Tasmanian Devil on speed. Here though, there was only really one boy who seemed disinterested and wandered a little, while everyone else was pretty on point, doing what they should be doing. Of course, when you have a large number of young kids singing together, it is pretty pitchy and the instrument playing is not polished, but it was great to see that these kids take it seriously, and some are really talented for their age. Very few of these kids will likely go on to actually be musical performers in the future, but I believe that they will probably have a pretty decent education in the classroom because they aren't continually distracted by other students, and their teacher can teach, rather than wrangle. In the later years it will start to diversify more, but I am glad that Smallsteps made the shift to the new school now, so that she gets a strong foundation and any help she might need, rather than ignored because she isn't a problem child. I am not sure what the focus is on in schools these days, but I feel that the spotlight should be on developing the skills necessary to successfully navigate the world and have the abilities to be a valuable part of the community. I think a lot of time and effort however is spent on trying to manage poor behaviours of some kids (not blaming the kids) rather than developing and growing the skillsets of all kids. I think there is too much required of school educators, because other parts of society are failing to teach the skills a child needs to manage. And I think that is another point of selection bias tonight, because looking around the auditorium at the parents, there also seems to be a weighting more toward parents who at least *look like* they take a more active role in parenting. I know for Smallsteps' close friends at this school, they don't spend time on phones and in front of screens nearly as much as those at her last school. > Does parenting make a difference? I suspect so. But at least, I think some kids go to school more prepared to perform than others, and when all are relatively prepared, the school environment is pretty healthy. When few are though, it becomes a process of behavioural mitigation, rather than supportive growth. Regardless, I enjoyed seeing her up on stage singing, and being so happy afterward. That's the highlight for me. Taraz [ Gen1: Hive ] --- **Be part of the Hive discussion.** - Comment on the topics of the article, and add your perspectives and experiences. - Read and discuss with others who comment and build your personal network - Engage well with me and others and put in effort **And you may be rewarded.** ---

links.body: >\n\nPresentamos la trayectoria de **Desorden Público**, la banda que desde 1985 transformó la escena venezolana con su \
