body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdynctatkvJeesq5BgcrKPWsftwGMCQYisJnKggkRyAhe/copia_de_1_.png)

Hello reflection hunters, how quickly the week has passed. Today I'm writing from a different place, but as always I begin by wishing you a beautiful and lovely morning. Well, it's morning here, but if where you're reading this it's another time, let's just call it a beautiful and lovely day. I also hope you've been able to capture some interesting reflection during these days. I captured two and today I share one with you. The first one was natural, and the second one, which I share today, is a photograph of a clover on a glass table. I hope you like my capture.
> Hola, cazadores de reflejos, qué rápido ha pasado la semana. Hoy escribo desde un lugar distinto, pero como siempre comienzo deseándoles una hermosa y linda mañana. Bueno, aquí es de mañana, pero si donde me lees es otra hora, mejor lo dejamos en un hermoso y lindo día. También espero que hayan podido capturar algún reflejo interesante durante estos días. Yo capturé dos y hoy les comparto uno. El primero fue de forma natural, y el segundo, el que hoy les comparto, es una fotografía de un trébol sobre una mesa de cristal. Espero que les guste mi captura.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSuz6DeuFMuqyPt7hmVUFJro5oAVMSmxHuAHJWtBzp2Do/20260327_170848.jpg)

As you well know, clovers are among my favorite plants, and although some consider them simple weeds, I see them as little magical sprouts. Whenever I see a clover plant, I can't resist searching among its leaves for one with four petals. And truth be told, I'm not very lucky at finding them. Perhaps the luck of four-petal clovers is finding them. I think that during the almost 3 years I've been here, I've shared a lot about clovers, from photographs to drawings, even a reflection here and there; therefore, I feel somewhat repetitive writing about the plant itself. Today I will focus on the photograph I took and its details. The first thing is how I took it: I took it on top of a glass table in a dark environment, lowering the camera's exposure almost to the minimum, so that the whole setting would darken and only the details of the plant's leaves and the reflection would remain visible. To achieve a more uniform green, I simply made some minimal adjustments in Snapseed. Also, when shooting, I tried to achieve the greatest possible depth with a foreground that is nicely out of focus, a very sharp midground, and a background with a slight blur, from the closest elements to the farthest ones. I really liked how the photograph turned out, and I think that along with the photo of the bougainvillea flowers, they are my favorites in the community. I hope you also like this photograph. For today, I say goodbye, wishing you, as always, all the luck and success in the world. Bye bye!
> Como bien saben, los tréboles son de mis plantas favoritas, y aunque algunos los consideran simples hierbajos, yo los veo como pequeños brotes mágicos. Siempre que veo una planta de tréboles no puedo resistirme a buscar entre sus hojas uno de cuatro pétalos. Y la verdad no tengo mucha suerte encontrándolos. Quizás la suerte de los tréboles de cuatro hojas es encontrarlos. Creo que durante los casi 3 años que llevo aquí he compartido mucho sobre tréboles, desde fotografías hasta dibujos, incluso alguna que otra reflexión; por lo tanto, me siento algo repetitivo escribiendo sobre la planta en sí. Me centraré en el día de hoy en la fotografía que tomé y sus detalles. Lo primero es la forma de tomarla: la tomé encima de una mesa de cristal en un ambiente oscuro, bajando la iluminación de la cámara casi al mínimo, para que todo el ambiente se oscureciera y solo quedaran visibles los detalles de las hojas de la planta y del reflejo. Para lograr un verde más uniforme, simplemente hice unos ajustes mínimos en Snapseed. Además, a la hora de disparar, traté de buscar la mayor profundidad posible con un primer plano bien desenfocado, un plano medio muy nítido, y un tercer plano con un ligero desenfoque, desde los elementos más cercanos a los más lejanos. La fotografía me gustó mucho cómo quedó, y creo que junto a la foto de las flores de bugambilia son mis favoritas en la comunidad. Espero que a ustedes también les guste esta fotografía. Por hoy me despido deseándoles, como siempre, toda la suerte y éxitos del mundo. ¡Chau chau!

If you found this article helpful or enjoyed reading it, I would greatly appreciate your comments. Best wishes!*_

Si encontraste este artículo útil o disfrutaste leyéndolo, agradecería enormemente tus comentarios. ¡Mis mejores deseos!_

The Holy Spirit's task is to find out our flaws, guide us toward repentance, and explain why our deeds are immoral and offensive to our God. The Holy Spirit provides us the resources and bravery to live morally, obey God, fullfil His laws, and combat off sins.

body.title: pre-plane thoughts, fever chills & my kind of guy
body.body: well, it's been a minute since i did a #ttt (ahoj, @ablaze!), but i thought today might be a good day, so here we go. i'm dressing up my dreams and stripping down my legs, looking back to where we were last year, while getting ready to board for the future.\n\nwe're going to spain in a hot minute (or rather, a hot day or two), and my immune system decided to take a swivel and a dive, so i'd have to think about something other than lounging on the beach. and being as i am part listen to your body's wisdom, part romanian grit, i'm busy racing my own luck here. \
, we say in my language, and it's the cheeky equivalent of \

. if i busy my mind with packing and my body with nice herbal brews, i'm bound to luck out in time. sorry mate, i got other plans. this time, last year? was krakow and very different thoughts about the future. life changes on a dime, and now? this time, this year, i'm just mostly excited to see people i ain't seen in a good, sweet year, and perhaps a day too long. the fact that this year's venue happens to be a stone's throw from the nice, sunny beach is just a side benefit. *ahem* oh, and speaking of sunny... https://youtu.be/IPaHv2sQASg?list=RDIPaHv2sQASg while nothing will compare to the original, of course, i happen to love johnny's smoky voice, and the way imelda soars through that bashful, initial silence. haunted? not yet, but i find, very appropriate given the circumstances. i'm taking long afternoons in the sun to boost my wellbeing. admittedly, it would go much better seaside, but i do my best. i was walking home just now, thinking about last year. all that's changed, much of it my own intrepid illusions and silliness. i'm silly now in different ways, and to think, and am i allowed? it seems all i do is change up my mind, and turn on my heels, like a turncoat, like a painted trout. i gotta say, i'm at the same time more and less excited than i was last year, in a strange way. i've a small feeling of distance from Hive lately, and what a surprise, especially compared to last year, when i was posting mostly every day. now, my attention splatters in other places, i realize at times, there are better places for my words. dissatisfaction or just ennui? and won't it go away the moment i land in alicante? i know myself too well to bet. i'm excited to see a place i've never been before. i'm excited to see again folk i've seen before and liked. i'm excited to forsake myself in the waves for a day or two, and crawl back to bed with sand between my toes. https://youtu.be/cBjLLcawVWQ?list=RDcBjLLcawVWQ is it just me or are all nothing but thieves songs the same? still, this here ain't half bad. if this makes less sense than i would like, i blame it on the feverishness and the headache that's been dogging my steps ever since i woke up. what i'm trying to say, buzzparty-wise, is i'm eager to reconnect with a sense of belonging and community that, for better or worse, has been part of my life for nearly a decade now. i'm the sort of person who thinks much about the past, and throughout all the memories, there was still, always, writing here. am i excited about growing the platform? frankly, i've got my doubts (i am, by nature, quite cynical), but that doesn't mean i'm not still excited in a way. less the thrill of honeymoon love, and more the enduring sense of ease of a long-time friend or a family get-together is the background of my packing thoughts. in between music, of course. https://youtu.be/y7dgEonmmko see you all in alicante :) (well, everyone who's coming, that is). i'm not in the habit of seeing people who aren't there. or at least, i know better than last time about saying so out loud. if there's one thing i would share with someone just discovering Hive for the first time, it'd be this. the way it's been there always, the sense of coming back here, of finding a kindly person to talk to, even more so than someone to read my winding thoughts. in a world where attention turns on a dime, i'd say that's not nothing, wouldn't you?

body.body:
>

### Hello hello silver bloggers, music lovers and Hello hivers! 

One of my favourite days because it means a post on Hive will be written by me, and I get to hear other music that Hiveians enjoy. Well for the select band that participate in ttt anyway!

Today we go back and listen to one of the pioneers of synth music!


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tengolotodo/23vrtjusxkFUGMnocz6gKynW2MX1eBNeU6VqzVBUXWuAwZRyPXjCDVNZGVtiqhacc3avU.png)


We are going back to my Silver Chronicles post of a few weeks ago [My Soundtrack for the 80s my favourite decade](https://peakd.com/hive-106316/@tengolotodo/my-soundtrack-for-the-80s)


Quite a self-explanatory title and it is my inspiration for the next few posts on ttt!

The year is now 1981 and we are diving into some poignant songs from Ultravox during their peak and final year together of 1981...

Who remembers Midge Ure and that wee pointed moustache thing of his!



***
It is Tuesday and that of course means that it's #ttt or #threetunetuesday and so it's time to share some tunes with you!
***
@ablaze started #ttt **257** weeks ago! Go check out what it is all about on his latest post [Ireland's Top 30 Songs of all Time (16, 17, 18) for Three Tune Tuesday - Week 256 - win some HBI](https://peakd.com/hive-193816/@ablaze/ireland-s-top-30-songs-of-all-time-16-17-18-for-three-tune-tuesday-week-256-win-some-hbi)

***Do go support @ablaze as without him we would not have this mental fun musical activity that you can win HSBI from! I am happy to be one of the SIX sponsors and it is kinda fun checking out music from all over this global village of ours!***

He has just released some winners posts, so go support those posts, he gets no support from any whales or even curation trails for these posts that he does. 255 weeks is an incredible amount of time, and I for one love that he runs this, and I appreciate the time and dedication that he puts in, when he could be doing something else.

### Long live #ttt 😁🎼 and #threetunetuesday

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tengolotodo/23tbREoadfKSsGzyuSnsFLq1mrjfW2mLAeRPZ5DB4jRPgi9K1U3x6qGyEsbyUibDr2s7P.png)

### The Band - Ultravox 

For this week’s #TTT, as I have alrady mentioned (if you were paying fluffing attention that is!) I’m taking us back to 1981. This was the year Ultravox truly conquered the airwaves. 

Following the departure of John Foxx, Midge Ure duly arrived. And this seemed to spark their fortunes as it transformed the band into a cinematic and melodic powerhouse. 

Their sound was a blend of cold industrial synthesisers and soaring romantic vocals of Midge Ure as we are about to hear.

Ultravox were fluffing true pioneers. While many bands were just starting to use keyboards, Ultravox used them to create huge orchestral masterpieces in a sense. With Billy Currie’s classically trained ear and Midge Ure’s pop nose, they bridged the gap between underground electronic music and mainstream success. 

1981 was truly their year, and all three of these tunes were released in 1981.

We have two lesser known of their songs following on from one of the most famous songs of 1981!



![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tengolotodo/23tbREoadfKSsGzyuSnsFLq1mrjfW2mLAeRPZ5DB4jRPgi9K1U3x6qGyEsc1VG2rdwmPg.png)


### Tune 1 - Ultravox - Vienna

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xJeWySiuq1I

You can’t talk about 1981 without this masterpiece.

In fact fluff it, you can't talk about Ultravox without mentioning Vienna!

Ironically tt famously held the #2 spot for weeks (kept off #1 by Joe Dolce of all people, with the bloody annoying song **Shaddap You Face**!)..

Well it outlasted its rivals in legacy. The haunting drum machine, the dramatic violin solo, and Midge Ure’s incredible vocal reach make this a stone-cold classic. 

It feels like a black-and-white film in musical form. I just loved their videos, awesome for their times!



![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tengolotodo/23tbREoadfKSsGzyuSnsFLq1mrjfW2mLAeRPZ5DB4jRPgi9K1U3x6qGyEsbyZ88cAchjQ.png)


### Tune 2 - Ultravox  - The Thin Wall

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yYGx00779f8

Released as a single from the Rage in Eden album later in '81, this track shows the darker and more experimental side of the band. They all seemed to do it at some point...

It’s got a driving energy and some fantastic synth textures that still sound modern today. It captures that feeling of tension and atmospheric art-rock that the band did better than anyone else.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tengolotodo/23tbPU2aSDgfDb3KWRiUFfKXE6TczjnuAsZxWdugka3Q49Viv17j6SQ6qj3D94ofTDSCY.png)


### Tune 3 - Ultravox - All Stood Still
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mW9ImnTL2jk

This was the final single from the Vienna album, and it’s a pure synth-pop floor-filler. I must admit it is a tossup as to whether I prefer Vienna or All Stood Still. 

It’s a bit more mechanical and robotic than the title track which highlighting Billy Currie’s legendary keyboard work. It also perfectly captured the \

aesthetic that defined the early 80s club scene.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tengolotodo/23tbREoadfKSsGzyuSnsFLq1mrjfW2mLAeRPZ5DB4jRPgi9K1U3x6qGyEsbyZ88cAchjQ.png)



### So there you have it 3 songs released in 1981 from Ultravox this week with my [80s Soundtrack post](https://peakd.com/hive-106316/@tengolotodo/my-soundtrack-for-the-80s) as the inspiration!




Which was your favourite tune? Or have you never heard of them?



![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tengolotodo/23tbREoadfKSsGzyuSnsFLq1mrjfW2mLAeRPZ5DB4jRPgi9K1U3x6qGyEsc1VG2rdwmPg.png)

I wish that you all have a brilliant happy fun and terrific Tuesday until we meet again enjoy your tunes 🎶🎵🎶

ApeCoin (APE) is turning heads across crypto Twitter right now and for good reason. After months of painful decline to a record low of $0.08, APE has exploded with a +22.39% move on the chart, hitting a 24 hour high of $0.1917 on massive volume of over 153 million APE traded. But this isn't a random pump three major catalysts hit at the same exact time.

Catalyst, 1  New CEO at Yuga Labs

Yuga Labs confirmed Michael Figge as the new CEO on April 24, right on the 5th anniversary of Bored Ape Yacht Club.   This is the most significant leadership change the company has had in over a year. Figge has signaled a clear shift in focus toward expanding the Otherside metaverse platform and rebuilding engagement around NFTs,  exactly what the community had been demanding for months.

Catalyst, 2 The $1 Million Whale Bet

Just before the breakout, a newly created wallet sold roughly 75 ETH worth approximately $174K and deployed over $1 million into a 5x leveraged long on APE via Hyperliquid, with an entry near $0.1047. That kind of high-conviction positioning in a low-liquidity token creates a chain reaction  other traders notice, FOMO kicks in, and the price accelerates.

Catalyst, 3  Supply Pressure Is Gone

By March 2026, roughly 90% of the 1 billion APE supply was already in circulation, meaning the two-year headwind of constant sell pressure from token unlocks is now behind the market. Less inflation with even slightly improving demand completely changes the equation for APE holders.

The Technical Picture

The 1H chart shows APE trading well above all three EMAs  EMA 25 at 0.1563, EMA 50 at 0.1523, EMA 100 at 0.1467. The descending parallel channel that had trapped price since October 2025 finally broke to the upside  the first clean structure break after months of lower highs. Volume confirms the move is real.

What's Next?

The key level to watch is $0.171 hold above it and the trade stays alive, with year-end targets pointing toward $0.363 as the base and $0.450 as the upper ceiling. Lose that level, and this quickly risks becoming a failed breakout. 
The real long term bet is ApeChain. If Yuga Labs successfully launches playable experiences in Otherside using ApeChain, this could create real demand for APE through gas fees, governance participation, ecosystem rewards, and metaverse usage rather than just speculative trading. 
APE was dead money for months. Now, with new leadership, a cleared supply overhang, and a whale going all in  things just got very interesting.

[![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSRbW6rFjv9tYaXWiU7eNeqoM4iWoZXx9VptQyqoq6PYd/13294109cd53d8a9d8128cf260466ff3)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=efootjoker-yt/5b375407)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=efootjoker-yt/5b375407)


---

---

<center>**Hello everyone and welcome back to my blog.**</center>

---
#

My next mission was to liberate the Ohama Fishing Village. There had been news that the village was now under the control of the Mongols. They were capturing innocent villagers and forcing them to work. So my job was to go there, drive out all the Mongol soldiers and rescue the villagers.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYtQdn9C9Sw4FcN6iwExFemEQHHkQjZSQRGTGFKdf59rz/snapshot_66.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQqXQVWucu6bNfcQBW6948Qc1PATjQqcXqcbQxsNfduAm/snapshot_67.png)

Since Ohama is a fishing village, it is located by the sea. When I reached there, I saw the red light of the sunset spreading all around. The whole place looked very beautiful. So I took a few pictures before starting the mission.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNWPVVpFAiKBdknduxoQB2RLtKWMrA9JTM5fL9hBsgwXm/snapshot_63.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXXZ7nA2bfjQW1ypwc6ZzUu6YbwCPZQbMPMw8SnCJU96X/snapshot_64.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmef6SKtmAom3w1xiR76661Jn5Mqs5scMi5KVyRL9QRtnj/snapshot_65.png)

Then I went inside and started the attack. The first thing I saw was an archer. I killed him with my bow. Then I climbed up a hut and looked around. I saw a few Mongol soldiers standing around a prisoner, along with two dogs.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRmKfGUt2E77gJa2Sp8nKSe4saFpPwJTmbqkPng64sxX5/snapshot_68.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXii2YFd9iHTj1G3Nv6bgGuthZUWp99spgxVe9rgR9Xyc/snapshot_69.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTXE9FV2VnBiJAMXeeq2qQbB3amiYiNbV1rjMW1LLF3ky/snapshot_70.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVzDxuyYWEfiZTgj3UvTCyC5JixjBp3WXLWt1grjZXVAw/snapshot_71.png)

I first tried to pull them aside, but the plan didn't work. So I jumped straight in. I jumped from above and killed one, then quickly finished off two more. One of the black dogs kept coming and biting me, so I took the opportunity to shoot it with an arrow. Then the soldiers surrounded me from all sides. But now my fighting skills have improved a lot. Perfect parry, dodge and quick attack, all together it was not difficult to handle them. I finished them off one by one and freed the prisoner. He thanked me and said that two other village elders were still imprisoned.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfLTbk611yYuuQnf8q7rbzGBVP9MuYWaniDeNTBxs1L7f/snapshot_72.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmU6TciE3bJrtJpcGC3zqj6kCCRAmefnyJTafyQPUhqioH/snapshot_73.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmY2uHKf57DxyyfLqtQBM3CPKJDsK4Zu8wMpSZNXhbYLBt/snapshot_74.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeZ5KkEF2xDeT3ESgPR4jJVwGiJioXcN1SVh9q46ANe4w/snapshot_75.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYEeidqiAzzhyBPj6YHUFBzS383Se8cTMF7nwUZpaivEi/snapshot_76.png)

I moved forward to the river. Three soldiers were guarding another Elder. Two of them had swords in their hands, one had a spear. I killed the spear soldier first, because his attacks were more dangerous. Then I threw a smoke bomb and finished off the other two with a chain assassination. Then I freed the second Elder. He was very happy, because he thought he would not survive.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWThsRai5oTWjsVwBVk3S3fbFVVrRhhyUQDhAmmqZ5A5z/snapshot_77.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVZN8EJdSFS9EatEGBWvfW7e73yJRhWzvdfmMbu7T5K3g/snapshot_78.png)

Let's go save the third Elder. This was the hardest part. About ten or twelve soldiers were surrounding him. Some had a spear, some a mace, some a bow, and some a sword.

So instead of attacking directly, I took a tactic. I saw that a few soldiers stayed with the prisoner, while the rest wandered around. Those who were alone, I quietly killed them one by one. No one even noticed.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbQAzvApyd7e9bZsk9FFyEcg2WUDCrSwSouHgDKgnksJq/snapshot_79.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZWSvMPtXYkNAo3vffra3pdgFmT3G5Bvmk9KmABJzcXKy/snapshot_80.png)

When there were a few left, I climbed onto the roof and threw a fireball down. Seeing the fire, everyone gathered there. This was the best opportunity. I jumped down and killed three of them in an instant with a chain assassination. When another one tried to run away in fear, I finished him off with an arrow from behind.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUC9r4Ehht3qWZ4QpXus7riqdVmuRvJ27Crq2JrtgLe4K/snapshot_81.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVohvpSDpPXKEEhcFwxec4yUGq5d7oap3SHCwGqtxjUam/snapshot_82.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma6qE7gAr3QWxvLtoRHLeEUAcLe1iH2ecXDnzDtm6aa3Y/screenshot_3024_.png)

Then I freed the third Elder. He thanked me and gave me a key called the Ohama Key. If you can collect six such keys, you can unlock Gosaku's Armor.

Finally, Ohama Fishing Village was completely free from the Mongols. The villagers returned one by one and started their normal lives again. And I was ready to free the next village.

---

* **See You All In My Next Post.**
* **I took all these screenshots while playing the game and the thumbnail was created in Canva.**

---

body.title: Are You Resilienced?
body.body:
>

I was meant to be on-site training, but due to some scheduling issues, the sessions have been remote instead. I far prefer to speak to people face to face, despite the convenience of being able to use more tools and the freedom of three screens to manage the session. Personal connection is vital in my opinion, and although many shy away from them more and more, I believe that it is going to cause a lot of problems in the future. 

---


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/23vsd7KzgVKMJ6HKAb1r47i9G6zmYCpev23bJcb8sW415Bm3qwaSpEWzXcaTZ28M6U4Lr.png)


---

And on this note, in the two sessions I have had so far, similar themes have come up, with the first being about how people today make \
, making larger problems out of minor issues, especially when it comes to taking offence. Rather than assuming best intentions, people are increasingly assuming the worst and then \

themselves based on the perceived slight.

In the next session the client was talking about an audit process that is coming up and how he believes that despite there being no issues in the past, he reckons that with new people now, there is a far greater risk because they have become complacent. They don't have the direct experience of those who have prepared for the audit in the past, but because everything has gone well, they assume it will go well again. 

> Skills missing. 

As I mentioned to them both is, what I see as part of the problem with many things today, where people don't have the direct experience, but have been given all the answers. I even ran a bit of a thought experiment where two children are raised, one normally, the other being spoon-fed everything, carried everywhere, etc. Essentially, one has to work for the answers, the other is given the results. What is the difference between the two?

And this is the issue, because while we might be able to get results cheaply, the value is actually in the *working.* It is pretty obvious that if a child is carried everywhere, their muscles will not develop, nor will they learn to crawl, walk or run. But, what most fail to understand is that the brain itself is a physical thing, even if the thoughts it has may not be. This means that the very structure of the brain is developed like other parts of the body, *though usage.* When only seeing the results, the brain doesn't develop the structure to *create the working.* 

Similarly, the more controlled our environment is, the more sensitive we become. And what we have done is created a very controlled environment that is managed by the enduser. The user chooses what they consume and convenience and pleasure tend to be the driving factors. This means that skills that are developed in difficult and boredom, don't get developed. Moreover, the ability to deal with discomfort is lessened, making us more sensitive to variation, and more volatile in reaction. 

Skills come in many forms but beyond innate talent, they need to be developed. To develop any skill, knowledge isn't enough, it requires practice. It doesn't matter if it is a physical skill like welding seams or surfing, a mental skill like critical thinking, or an emotional skill such as patience and reactivity. And then of course, there are the myriad social skills for interpersonal communication, that allow us both to transmit ideas, and receive them. 

The way we have designed our environment has meant that some skills are far more developed than others. For instance, emotional sensitivity is high, but emotional management is low. If we imagine the same in terms of our body, it is like always skipping leg day. Brain function is similarly unbalanced, where we consume so many \

but spend so little time generating results from our own thoughts, that we are losing the ability to problem-solve - which is one of the greatest functions we have at our disposal as humans. 

The thing is though, that like the companies who are cutting costs to increase profit margins, without working out how to generate new revenue, we  are using these tools to make our life easier at the expense of our skills, without working out how to generate additional value as a human. Our profit margin is the amount of convenience and entertainment we get, instead of what we are able to actually do. 

I believe that most people who are leaning into getting \
now, are going to make themselves worse off in the future. This isn't necessarily going to be noticeable to begin with, because being \

gets rewarded, but eventually, efficiency without the ability to generate growth, means retraction. Many companies now, despite their business retracting, are increasing their valuation. This is a disconnection from reality, a bubble. But ultimately, people will keep chasing for fear of missing out, even if they know it is going to lead them to failure. We are weakening ourselves as a species across the board and the irony is, most of us believe we are strengthening. Another irony is that even though we are so more emotionally sensitive, we don't have the experience or intelligence to recognise the folly of our ways. >The audit is coming. *Are you resilient enough?* Taraz [ Gen1: Hive ] --- **Be part of the Hive discussion.** - Comment on the topics of the article, and add your perspectives and experiences. - Read and discuss with others who comment and build your personal network - Engage well with me and others and put in effort **And you may be rewarded.** ---

# Lilac Blossom

I had to google that.
I never came across the word _lilac_.
...very common around here. (We call it _Flieder_)
Smells even better than it looks.

![IMG_20260428_120940.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/felixxx/23xAMA4aJgUmjroR27umi1y2FQ89E2GwcSD6gcRbXqN6qgsXvecZn95wV2Jwt8ugf2vss.jpg)

# Jobs done

- planting potatoes
- planting corn
- weeding
- mowing (again)

the usual stuff...

![IMG_20260428_122127.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/felixxx/23xVEe3jkuR5D1H5B2jJLMkaRmpRFKAE39s4bq4w97kXqtRcPTLjMnXRTJWkik5C7Le6f.jpg)

# Anyways

I think I have finally fixed [the wood chipper](/@felixxx/replacement-clutch).
I actually found an old rusty M20 nut, sawed some of it off and it fits.

![IMG_20260428_113641.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/felixxx/EogNkFY8gNoNApLe9fQfzJVjzkLubQKSTZRgKby9nWnBXh6BtzZ6EhFz8N9Mdg2kbVW.jpg)

## Hackjob

I also had to drill a hole in the thing, just so I can stick something in there, so that I can actually tighten the bolt, without turning the whole driveshaft with it.

I butchered half the piece trying to drill into it. 
I could not get the drill any closer and had to drill at an angle and the thing kept spinning until I strapped it with cable ties.

Cringe.

![IMG_20260427_111053.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/felixxx/23w2gcCPALk6nTcq4V7xmp1DsRVnVXDVVSP7p673L28GvpSVhZZmjwWaHLWPe57ShxA48.jpg)

# test run

I put it all together and fired up the engine and the clutch engaged.
Great success!

Observing this happen for the first time, I'd say: the clutch engaged from the first moment, instantly. Makes me wonder, how important it really is...

![IMG_20260428_113653.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/felixxx/Eoptr3n4g1ybKixvXiXf5nSua7jcCqmioFj4XV6UiUj1ghGae7NtuvEDbevYoARDGYP.jpg)

# Help

I still need a new belt and the nut is still a little too thick, so I have to take it all apart again.
Then, putting it back together properly, I need a second pair of hands, because I can't pull the engine block to tension the belt and tighten the screws for it at the same time.

What a hassle...

body.title: How Do You Troubleshoot Cloud Network Failures in the Google Network Engineer Exam?
body.body:
The Google Professional Cloud Network Engineer Exam evaluates how effectively you can identify and resolve network-related issues in complex cloud environments. Candidates are often presented with scenarios involving connectivity failures, routing issues, firewall misconfigurations or hybrid network disruptions. Success depends on understanding how Google Cloud networking components interact and how traffic flows between virtual networks, on-premises systems and external services.  
**Common Challenges in Troubleshooting Scenarios**  
Many candidates struggle because cloud networking problems are often layered and not immediately obvious. A single issue may involve DNS configuration, VPC settings or security rules working together. The exam tests your ability to analyze symptoms, identify the root cause and choose the most efficient fix. Without hands-on experience, it becomes difficult to prioritize which component is causing the failure.

Get Started Now: [https://www.pass4success.com/google/exam/professional-cloud-network-engineer](https://www.pass4success.com/google/exam/professional-cloud-network-engineer)  
  
**Key Troubleshooting Focus Areas**  
  
To handle these scenarios effectively, candidates should focus on core networking concepts frequently tested in the exam:  
  
**.** VPC configuration and subnet routing  
**.** Firewall rules and access control policies  
**.** Load balancing and traffic distribution issues  
**.** DNS resolution and connectivity validation  
**.** Hybrid connectivity using VPN or Interconnect  
  
Mastering these areas helps you quickly narrow down the source of network failures.  
  
**Problem-Solving Approach for Exam Success**  
  
A structured troubleshooting method is essential when answering Google Network Engineer Exam Questions. Start by identifying the symptoms, then isolate the affected network layer and finally test possible causes step by step. Eliminating incorrect options logically helps you reach the most accurate solution. Understanding how each networking component affects overall connectivity is key to making correct decisions under exam pressure.  
  
**Strengthening Your Preparation Strategy**  
  
Consistent practice with real-world scenarios is crucial for success. Working through different network failure cases improves your analytical thinking and speed in identifying root causes. Reviewing mistakes and understanding why certain solutions are correct will significantly enhance your performance. Many candidates also explore platforms like Pass4Success to access additional practice materials and gain better insight into exam patterns, helping them prepare more effectively.

body.body:
[![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmddrTL2CrfYiNWob7Ct83NEV2YKirXCTbWHwauLeCxMvw/094986c061d8cb25d9b61ca470146ad1)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=angelmitu/b38d671f)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=angelmitu/b38d671f)


---

Hello friends, welcome everyone.How are you all? I hope everyone is well.Today I have come up with another artist of my daughter.Today he tried to build a small dwelling with his hands.Where there is a house and a coconut tree.There is also the brightness of the sun.He tried to portray it with pen and different colored pencils.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRwTE1N5QnmViY821uJdVRzaeNaUBo4aWRZ8H8Mwjrz1Y/img_20260428_wa0009.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmc7TZjB3CFUSPJkEDDBw4LdMsKr6dKo7M4ExW5FTn2M8Y/img_20260428_wa0008.jpg)

My daughter is currently undergoing her exams.She has seven exams and six of them have been completed today.There is an oral exam tomorrow.The written exams are over, so today after the exams, he came home and wanted to do some art.It's raining today, so he expressed his desire to do some art on this rainy day.Then he created a small dwelling with color pencil.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTtk1GY2DqK9BWhW5XXLGheSV1uBXRoKMmcoH76Re9Rtf/img_20260428_wa0007.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXt1Km3DZ1XTXiwGemGtfqEDb9kUYShxgG6dYWyc38qyc/img_20260428_wa0006.jpg)

If children want to do handicrafts along with their studies, then it is good.Because in the current era of social media and internet, it is good to do handicrafts to keep them away from social media.Besides it's raining today, so he try to do the art at home with colored pencils, which is a good attempt.It's good to do these things along with studying.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfM4H2CjW7zkjjJnG142tse4QcVKQak4y9VEJQhTEN76N/img_20260428_wa0000.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUm5WyEWRb7eEyHNtdVhy2YAG8yAfNaSJRABuFSr5HvGH/img_20260428_wa0001.jpg)

Besides I told him some stories from our childhood that when we were little, we didn't have any mobile phones or internet.Then he asked me how we used to spend our time.Then I said that we listened to fairy tales and played by making different things in the clay.But the fairy tales and scenes of making things out of clay are lost today.Hearing my story, he was inspired to do some art.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmb4AdvGRbr3L4eQbUw7txqUva9fqp4ApkfysiWvUscRp7/img_20260428_wa0002.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmen4f27en43rySerzQ5uXxhbdpHbpz62kXorfyrHJnie8/img_20260428_wa0003.jpg)

Along with her studies, she was inspired to do art and I was the cameraman.And it's my job to see the good and bad of my daughter, so I always try to do what's best for her.First he drew a house and a coconut tree with a black pen.The sun peeks out from behind the house.Then he colored them with his coloring pencils.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmddrTL2CrfYiNWob7Ct83NEV2YKirXCTbWHwauLeCxMvw/img_20260428_wa0004.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSD7gN3fD6yLZ5EuYSfBujs89KBPvDUbY3jCGrS2bdr32/img_20260428_wa0005.jpg)

His artist scene today is very beautiful and I liked it so I shared it with you.The entire art making scene is shown in the video.

Thank you.

@Angelmitu

body.title: Sweet Potato and Avocado Tart
body.body:
> ![20260422_124532.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23z7G4afTRXq9m31Eq2yn9GoYcczendw8PGy9iQ8dEhFG5sVouWDHX5VhcessFyzauLkj.jpg)
Vegan dishes always have a story behind every meal served—the story of how they were prepared. It’s a story that will be remembered forever. Behind the preparation of this simple dish is my husband, who is always enthusiastic about every meal I serve at home. Especially with the unique flavor profile, it makes him very happy to try my new creations. Well, this time it’s something different—a super easy vegan dish using flour-free ingredients. It’s definitely very healthy since it’s simply baked. This recipe features sweet potatoes and a delicious avocado filling.
Sweet Potato Avocado Tart
![20260422_124739.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23xL4sGb2QmPt6eFRwWqTbdg9R47T6FsJesLynghci2UNqtfrxfHchnuxQGqANVqBmSfJ.jpg) The sweet potato avocado tart is a baked tart made with sweet potatoes combined with oats. Of course, it features a tempting filling made from blended avocado. The topping of roasted peanuts makes this dish truly amazing. Curious about the steps? Let’s check out the recipe below.
Ingredients
![20260422_091441.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/EprUWu41e8ymTJLvSuvgy3jWTx65hcZ4JkBGomR4qwN6jkENrerTioP5FuB4avLDvcH.jpg)
350 grams sweet potato 3 tablespoons oats 1 avocado Salt to taste Granulated sugar to taste (optional)
Instructions
Boil the sweet potatoes until tender, then mash them while still hot until smooth. Add the oats and stir until well combined; you may add a pinch of salt.
| ![20260422_091603.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23x1HQJR1yLXnUW1C4ePYpbnhvx57uHBXqGfb7GgMokB7ebQQwz732UAQXzfpscpgVhxq.jpg) | ![20260422_091616.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wWyQ2CMX3vGSx63qvJi77NgNPMQTdQ5CcV43qYw812DES4SXYgqe4Tu3JzrJrF37qPR.jpg) | ![20260422_091632.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23x19JGwj8aVVWB5L77M6MT43pcerpfC29PdRWQeWd5HskRRiijHMRtTHLHmvmjRDPpqy.jpg) | |-|-|-|
Press the mixture into a round baking pan—don’t forget to line it with parchment paper—and make sure to leave some space in the center when pressing it down.
| ![20260422_091724.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wX33f5o8F3rQVUiGqSbM6cBWccywdorLxehYVh57rSZC3pM4tPAEKMcroZvLqYtoN5P.jpg) | ![20260422_092246.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23yJLXP32VhsuZYgSdTWDYucbx8KEfkWE6Eqw8dzHa4DR5VqsgPgYAeWCv1cdyyYNweDh.jpg) | ![20260422_092225.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/243BnzockWQarxXPquukckbmGk9C14gYRXuTwwL8mBtQ7GeBujJQ6KzMTfZe217GHWf32.jpg) | |-|-|-|
Then bake in the oven until done, about 30 minutes on both top and bottom heat.
| ![20260422_094144.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23w2o8432EUmuNncALbvzCutynCohE7vU6y7w1cGCrTyapM91J5Fs3tCHt6TMqKSsqHZd.jpg) | ![20260422_100855.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23xVKS8XwXj5yAfeGJhk1VbU1eSvXXw5tzfmX3JYG46ALp38Eb5DgwthuQhKjsti6gPoS.jpg) | ![20260422_103637.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wgYdxeNFySsWCnNK6mNfdgo5qq14y2tF9jwXmTKRVmd2iVhSAQXGRiGSfkTtonNH3Xq.jpg) | |-|-|-|
Next, I mix the avocado with a little sugar—just one teaspoon, though you can skip it. Add salt, then blend until smooth.
| ![20260422_092256.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wgPvLFZpuAzJA86UPpJARktAdeJdQDQ753ceYpMRkStEu1oJwkjCsJJXutZ5JFuNSAX.jpg) | ![20260422_092529.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wMcg4niLNvfmLSh68MnsFVb8dM1YsUSHow8KYrTktoGVYD3bGQmCPibaeqVwk1YQmgM.jpg) | ![20260422_093028.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wMcbd9vU3zmH5dt9Eg7Bg6eXqSvPZXYU9HjjUJLBg8CoQ1rRW99JnvnPRAstUnCCo5D.jpg) | |-|-|-|
Once the tart has cooled, add the avocado and sprinkle with the nut topping. Refrigerate or freeze for about 20 minutes to set.
| ![20260422_093449.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23x1BcHLFE6i8Hy46NvXpFoX7mJge2f66uDLUFr3rLiAzYny221VDUz8zGr82NgfF6xyZ.jpg) | ![20260422_103812.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wC9LmVednKVJHM7GHZCeoDu4KHAeRzPz72X48WrgHsSQDfuybxPWRNnqjcUQaLXzAfT.jpg) | ![20260422_103850.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23t7jDemvXtNz1CW4Qh9Ca9HDEMZaEcGJ3gFkNLKUVKNuNDxn6pW91eweBTWED5UYd6dS.jpg) | |-|-|-|
Result
![20260422_125000.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23ynjD2vdW6pPo3SWCWDGZXjmRm9xtcYFWHY5YhZCpng3zEpwkBmzMbEHcgijFdxj8a7a.jpg)
Ta-da! The result after taking it out of the freezer is absolutely beautiful—the avocado has set perfectly and is ready to enjoy. I tried cutting a slice—it’s set, and the result is truly that beautiful. The baked sweet potato layer is also excellent; I really love the texture. Plus, the avocado is so beautiful that anyone will love it. Just look at the combination of the light green avocado layer meeting the orange sweet potato—they blend perfectly.
|![20260422_124956.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wqxtxwzd2fA7vnBgWqWaUweHGGLZ8kp6pxgQ6wTVQxkYZYiba5PfcVtavDLmQWANsGE.jpg)|![20260422_124835.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wqrfMteKa2JxTUgzC4KwfMnJkswpbprHboN9PJM1f5mGZVWx5v8LRjAsEfkAY3tHVB3.jpg)|![20260422_124831.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23xyWzuBuaqWD68jthba1hmY5TaExXDMk9h2jkLRQFzVo72XTye2ZG4vG66WSwMyg2rHN.jpg)| |-|-|-| |![20260422_124913.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23x1Mi4UeaBML8FJLtenRBGPtt7u5uSg5ggwDCjEYzr5a3QSrKXC8gYfQ6z4QmEvAsmhx.jpg)|![20260422_125015.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wCJSbRJbap4fqM7e6t53vrW4D3F7RHSQgJCnzp6buU8sWUwVoCHdnfW8jaFmyWM1wAu.jpg)|![20260422_125033.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23yTqj47zftEPfGL2stmMGXuDaFPDfjbsY6ehQ35JiMEXtsFjVBKtyygZtjpq6Lnitk6U.jpg)|
As for the taste, there’s no doubt—it’s delicious. The sweet potato layer isn’t hard because I intentionally baked it so it wouldn’t be hard. The sweet potato layer is soft with an oat texture that makes it more varied. The best part of this is the avocado layer—it’s so delicious, with a soft texture and a very light sweetness. I really love it and can finish it in an instant.
![20230813_094117_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23ynhM4HY26LsJBc56VnzHwHASWwNh2k6eRFsTW3ZB37BNXHsDPbYNJn7HniS1Ky4w7Ki.png)

> ![20240420_153413.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23xybJaDM9iJEac2d34ghVhwHTLJQ2LkMrCFUTk1gbXyPNb8JzZk9mvDrrsvBt1wnEFYU.jpg)
About The Author
Welcome to this blog, I have a real name \

, who comes from Indonesia. I have several hobbies, reading, writing, gardening, I also love food and cooking, even art related.  And the most interesting one is spending the whole day traveling. From those hobbies, I will share some inspiring content for all of you, I hope you like my blog, please and reblog this post if you like it!.</sub>

body.title: Cuando el miedo te crea obstáculos que no están/When fear creates obstacles that are not there [ESP/ENG]
body.body: > Hola queridos amigos de @holoslotus, saludos y bendiciones, en esta ocasión vengo para hablarles sobre un tema que tuve tras hablar con mis primas en lo que respecta al miedo de poder avanzar o hacer algo que quieres, ciertamente un tema que nos hace reflexionar y ser capaces de comprender que el miedo no solo nos permite estar alerta también puede ocasionar que dejemos de hacer algo o cumplir un sueño por el simple hecho de no dar un paso hacia adelante. --- ![REVIEW (10).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23x1KZdruWyBDikV2AodmZEfECaArvMGYXjnTox1vk1yXim479m7dtcHCSyiQ4LQt6AGd.jpg) **Diseño en CANVA** ---

> En la vida siempre habrá circunstancias que nos den miedo el hecho de avanzar, sea tomar una decisión, hablar, hacer algo que quería, por el simple hecho de pensar tanto en el qué dirán, o que ocurrirá o que pasará si hago o digo eso, dejando de esta manera que el miedo te consuma y no puedes avanzar, ciertamente hay cosas que son inevitables sentir miedo como cuando decides comenzar desde cero, se siente como que todo lo que has hecho queda estático, como que siente si podrás hacerlo, es un riesgo, pero en la vida hay que tomar ciertos riesgos, si analizas la situación si vez los pro y contra, ¿Por qué no intentarlo? ![separadoryasma1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23tRzwswFj7sdCJKFgW2jsAWvCyEzuv6zxT8pCrVwXa8ePqRSdQWi3P6ZbtsyGmy6y4G2.png)

> Suena sencillo, pero en realidad tomar iniciativa nunca es fácil, sobre todo si está presente el miedo como una barrera que te obstaculiza para ver realmente todo el panorama, para apreciar lo que tienes al frente y para poder estar fresca y consciente de lo que quieres hacer, es como una piedra en el camino que si no sabes esquivar te puede lastimar más de lo que piensas, porque aunque creas que estas evitando algo que quizás te haga mal, también está la posibilidad que sea todo lo contrario y por miedo a dar el paso hacia delante ps resulta que no pudiste obtener algo mejor. --- ![geralt-man-4079511_1920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23t797twTXtJwkaUYyCutVgKJSBM1bZc9uUSs8E9kp5p1Xijsc5EZQWiqsYRaxpLHdrCK.jpg) [Fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/images/download/x-4079513_1920.jpg) ---

> La vida es sencillamente un cruce de muchos caminos, en donde no siempre las cosas están del todo claro, sobre todo cuando nos dejamos llevar por el miedo, por el intentar ver más allá de lo que queremos, porque pensamos que hasta ahí es donde debemos llegar, no somos capaces demás y es ahí el error, como dije antes si el miedo puede en su momento ser una espada que nos permita estar alerta en ciertas ocasiones pero también es una barrera que te puede cerrar por completo aquellos nuevos caminos que te pueden dar la oportunidad de aspirar a algo mejor, a darte cuenta lo que en verdad puede funcionar, hasta en la felicidad a veces se tiene miedo de ser completamente feliz, porque sientes que es efímeras o que no la mereces, puede ese miedo no puede impedir que la pueda disfrutar, a veces en la cosas más simples se queda uno estancando por el simple hecho de tener miedo a lo que vendrá, a un futuro incierto. ![separadoryasma1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23tRzwswFj7sdCJKFgW2jsAWvCyEzuv6zxT8pCrVwXa8ePqRSdQWi3P6ZbtsyGmy6y4G2.png)

> **Muchas gracias por leerlo. Espero sea de su agrado. Cualquier comentario con gusto estaré para responder y si quieren saber más de mi les dejo mis:**
![EL FINAL DE POSTHIVE (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23tmBcG1dhAWXHSeTXHGahwcGe8eAbcEpZutQrCnSNiXxDwJJ31QA17giTgLpxPgJtEqN.jpg)
![separadoryasma1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23tRzwswFj7sdCJKFgW2jsAWvCyEzuv6zxT8pCrVwXa8ePqRSdQWi3P6ZbtsyGmy6y4G2.png) **ENGLISH**

> Hello dear friends of @holoslotus, greetings and blessings, on this occasion I come to talk to you about a topic that I had after speaking with my cousins ​​regarding the fear of being able to move forward or do something you want, certainly a topic that makes us reflect and be able to understand that fear not only allows us to be alert, it can also cause us to stop doing something or fulfill a dream for the simple fact of not taking a step forward. --- ![REVIEW (12).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23x1KZdrvxCpKZSn2BQBPUtAw1FdENtS1ezt6Y3sga87ShGA15AGuFRPgFeufGXY1ZQpZ.jpg) **Design in CANVA** ---

> In life there will always be circumstances that make us afraid to move forward, be it making a decision, speaking, doing something you wanted, for the simple fact of thinking so much about what they will say, or what will happen or what will happen if I do or say that, thus letting the fear consume you and you cannot move forward, there are certainly things that are inevitable, feeling afraid like when you decide to start from scratch, it feels like everything you have done remains static, like you feel if you can do it, it is a risk, but in life you have to take certain risks, if you analyze the situation and see the pros and cons, why not try it? ![separadoryasma1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23tRzwswFj7sdCJKFgW2jsAWvCyEzuv6zxT8pCrVwXa8ePqRSdQWi3P6ZbtsyGmy6y4G2.png)

> It sounds simple, but in reality taking initiative is never easy, especially if fear is present as a barrier that hinders you from really seeing the whole picture, from appreciating what you have in front of you and from being able to be fresh and aware of what you want to do. It is like a stone on the road that if you do not know how to avoid it can hurt you more than you think, because even if you think you are avoiding something that may harm you, there is also the possibility that it is the opposite and for fear of taking the step towards front ps turns out you couldn't get something better. --- ![geralt-man-4079511_1920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23t797twTXtJwkaUYyCutVgKJSBM1bZc9uUSs8E9kp5p1Xijsc5EZQWiqsYRaxpLHdrCK.jpg) [Source](https://pixabay.com/es/images/download/x-4079513_1920.jpg) ---

> Life is simply a crossroads of many paths, where things are not always completely clear, especially when we let ourselves be carried away by fear, by trying to see beyond what we want, because we think that that is where we must go, we are not capable of anything else and that is the error, as I said before, if fear can at the time be a sword that allows us to be alert on certain occasions, but it is also a barrier that can completely close off those new paths that can give you the opportunity to aspire. to something better, to realize what can really work, even in happiness sometimes you are afraid of being completely happy, because you feel that it is ephemeral or that you do not deserve it, that fear cannot prevent you from enjoying it, sometimes in the simplest things you stay stuck for the simple fact of being afraid of what will come, of an uncertain future. ![separadoryasma1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23tRzwswFj7sdCJKFgW2jsAWvCyEzuv6zxT8pCrVwXa8ePqRSdQWi3P6ZbtsyGmy6y4G2.png)

> **Thank you very much for reading it. I hope you like it. I will be happy to respond to any comments and if you want to know more about me, I will leave you my:**
![EL FINAL DE POSTHIVE (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23tmBcG1dhAWXHSeTXHGahwcGe8eAbcEpZutQrCnSNiXxDwJJ31QA17giTgLpxPgJtEqN.jpg)
**Translated Using Deepl** ![separadoryasma2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23t7FGdvDtjjEnDiEmhiBDnp6mbsh7xtMBUvkUFiwLtYYSHA9MCnR3VGBuvWJeHNVDBGh.png)

body.title: The colors are my hobby and imagination

body.title: Dimitrie Gusti National Village Museum
body.body: **Yes, it's true! Guilty as charged... Once again, I'm a few weeks behind when it comes to sharing my travel escapades on my favorite blockchain. Let my excuse be that in Alicante, you’ll get a little sneak peek into what I’ve been up to lately. Volunteer guinea pigs, that is. But anyway, on to today's post. It's from Easter. The \

one, since Bucharest otherwise celebrates the Orthodox one later. At first, I thought my love was taking me to a Village People concert (partly because in a nearby park, Michael Jackson has his own avenue, right next to a Japanese garden swarming with Insta People; welcome to the globalized world!), but alas, no. No YMCA.**

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmY1VbdsxL3sYUrcYmUXhYgdhHdHZb2BgyzTBh9AUd8xaj/img_3053.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPx8AZXbFuCKGb8bsSsNfcmS8KASCECie5rdFyEW1qvhT/img_3054.jpg)


The Dimitrie Gusti National Village Museum is a massive open-air ethnographic museum. You'll definitely bump into people from small towns and villages here, especially at the various markets they host. Like the markets just before March 1st, when Romania celebrates the Mărțișor holiday and gentlemen buy little brooches, bracelets, and other trinkets by the dozen for every woman they know. Or the Easter markets, which, frankly, weren't much to write home about. Luckily enough, the museum has plenty to offer on its own.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbW4G5YBkp1TYaKd1YEvUAmPAtqxiL9qRAPAdVV85hM7o/img_3010.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbZXJjA9rTzj9aNZaR5ppWd1AwycyiooPdUYLNC8Hrd2M/img_3011.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdnSE3f7UW9ML8ovB2Y187JMbRndNdAkuJgGehBMRb1BV/img_3016.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTp6dHX4KSaRayytNqGXbdSpr5sbmESMrCwnBJkz12Mwt/img_3017.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYtvJHifPQGJFxx59z8jY3V48NB4ySARUnkD9A3RM66Lg/img_3012.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYU5pGbEWSyxhNSZn1ubtj7Da2fC5h6DLUfdm5JcaGmSQ/img_3013.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmS141JXz3wHLx98hu97D8D8aAE6ryKaYPAtJ3goZJzyxJ/img_3014.jpg)





There are over a hundred historical houses here from various Romanian regions. Although... on the edge of the museum, there are a few ruins that look a bit like squats. Hard to say if those are included in the official headcount. You can actually step inside many of the houses and feast your eyes on their authentic furniture and fittings. But you have to get there earlier than we did. Apparently, the houses close earlier than the rest of the museum. I do appreciate, however, that every house you can enter comes with its own guard, who is equally authentic. They will speak to you only in Romanian, or in the universal sign language of bored museum and gallery attendants. You might even be treated to the most frequently used phrase in this global tongue (wait, is it still a tongue?): **\

*

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmar8MGgYwQ7t359S1Fcz5bMQnm8V5GeSRwoS1tCagtxjx/img_3018.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmREC7jRR7SsCM8MEsE9dYLzav3g7wLwYj89uRWnQSDq6f/img_3020.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmP3rMRJxP6KXdK28jU2f9fXcpJxdDK4CjhcobZoZzSUFR/img_3026.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbn2sn3bsGtUpUtALR3ZtAJrndTeDiqbe6SymD7PRUwLA/img_3027.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmV9hcpASYyd9YJgiepcqfH3U4SZnCjFTxpoBYvkV4W33y/img_3028.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcqpz2GCQWk6YppR35YcEqmwWtB4aZsun6EnVK51hRS7E/img_3029.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZ3V8ugbgPXFnqywseEGdQFNX8bBNLpVztWa3mcRTJgsA/img_3030.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRhGkQW1BXwEcCa7jh9zB4L4mwHMxn1vs3PLngmrmXLR8/img_3031.jpg)



Anyway, the museum is definitely worth a visit. You’ll need about two hours to wander through it. Probably half that if the guards happen to be feeling grumpy and won't let you into any of the houses for no particular reason. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNQiWPtwEiDPEak5q1sTqkdagR8kVzXwCUBA9kzqWa6QP/img_3046.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVDxgYAsddcGp6evV5Lngbiytf8mUnjMTFVdJfbL6J8Hh/img_3047.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQTx9FXgU45gb3imL9K9rKe4ZrCKfKHFGQCB3pWJsErur/img_3048.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaxCNqXaipQfEFzESJs5uSXGDm5ZUVd7CdAw4K5APPwRe/img_3049.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQ2cfXoDEUvL51qBYj4FQfeedtyn5kkf9VQP21jnuzzPP/img_3051.jpg)



What struck me the most was how obvious it is from rural Romanian architecture that the Industrial Revolution reached this corner of Europe much later than, say, Austria-Hungary (and even they were pretty late to the party).

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmU1J9gF5TxiwCjBT3pZ4W98rGUkV48ZhM5eCHJrgP7aYh/img_3057.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUtrD3QSSQA9c8B5999ZmrMVnVa8o5VdHyThcrZH9zixp/img_3059.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmd76RiPCAZ7ovXV2iTMviRWNJHwUSobiUWz3sqfdGFHoo/img_3060.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNf49ws6wLpVzPKyoW4CzDpEZdTdVKeyFpA4iA77qknuA/img_3062.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXAV2N5ETTSLMYBqhwSR18eNPELDRcyM5vXhw4eEX1ggL/img_3063.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUQhpoceZDwTzF24JGKh6JxY5Z62DSfReqCQjNCXRMCKT/img_3064.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfFSgo5JKg6tt5Kq8QFXZ4Hw5wGjxFdJLA27ZupcraJad/img_3065.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPhmZgdpCE3ft2JRvAaNiuykNBx5GbHh83wDdZvwM9wH5/img_3066.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYNM3xcEKA9TvrJJ2ctfRp431dHVaoFVgfJZPPT4pZaUC/img_3067.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXAQLdrRDCxAT2ifiYnzXjLQM1bNvVRhoMYJ5vo7mDsZF/img_3068.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRdJXotDTQuVtK6YehmY5V1bBo3eUhFppenrcGj9B1JjY/img_3052.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmY1VbdsxL3sYUrcYmUXhYgdhHdHZb2BgyzTBh9AUd8xaj/img_3053.jpg)



And then, of course, there were the little wooden churches. Two of them. One was padlocked shut (whoever wishes to pray, let them do so under the open sky, just like in the days of the Lord of Hosts), while the other, thankfully, was accessible. Praise be to modern technology! The church was authentically unlit, but my phone can pull off great photos even with a mere sliver of light. The pictures actually reveal way more than we could see with the naked eye. Funny, having to snap a photo of the ceiling just so we could look at it.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYX4r6mihdkWiEnTh5kzudnHpMHD3EzzEKQzbrvysETX6/img_3035.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmePSxhd76m2euTFkRj5WrwEh3AdTkKRMWRsrWQ4QWY5Cx/img_3032.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNngEmvema8zihVop3gv5rqxbdVWNNnf56ryWRhmkQDFn/img_3033.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfHz4QFnYcssrL8SZiR8hNhcHo9pPYtg6p2jGdZWAVFGj/img_3034.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmda4T7HAuuHkJ63L546nxRLH4aHHycFJHUfHvSPGRzaxN/img_3055.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeeH3Jr6iVHVJ1ndoWeT7puoXoiSKjRJ5q73zsNMpT1vU/img_3056.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmac7zQ4ciqNndod8Fv5RukVgU4EMaqjbMRtU7B7WxWSCG/img_3061.jpg)

I was curious and immediately looked for information about this insect on Google and it turned out that this was a mealybug. body.title: Wondering and Wandering | Reflection
body.body:
/>

Reflection can be channelled to both the negative side that weighs down the mind with a series of regrets and the positive side that lights up the mind. Oftentimes, I engage in the positive side of it, and that occurs very often, even during my working hours...I just launch my mind into the deep sea of memories, reminiscing the good moments of my life, laughing at how I made some foolish moves, special moments with family, and reliving so many sweet thoughts.

As for the negative aspect, I do engage in it, no lies, but not often, and that is because I don't want to disturb my mind with thoughts of negative events that have happened or scenes I am expecting in the future...such as death scenes which I know will happen one day. Funny enough, most times this negative side of this helps to prepare the mind for what's to come and also helps someone to avoid making bad decisions from lessons learnt in the past.

The last time I reflected:

Like I said in the beginning, I seldom engage in moody, physical reflection; my mind does it for me while other parts of my body are engaged in different activities. Yes, it works for me like that. Also, my reflection does not just settle on the past, I take myself into the future, imagining scenes. Most times they are good scenes, and sometimes bad ones appear and anytime the bad ones appear, I can only imagine them briefly and leave quickly.

I remember a particular relationship I was in. On the night of Valentine’s Day, this lady’s line went off as early as 7 pm, and they always had electricity, which meant it was not because her phone battery died. That night, I was lost in deep, hurtful thoughts, assembling together the warning signs I had noticed earlier but ignored before that day. Music was playing in my ears, but none of it worked its magic on me, I was completely lost in thought, pondered, wondered and wandered(inwardly) but nothing positive came out.  
Do you want to know how it ended that day? That is a story for another day. Lol😅

When it comes to reflecting on negative things, I shy away from it a lot, but it still comes occasionally.

* * *

* * *

A few days ago, while pressing clothes with my headphones plugged into my ears and music playing, my mind drifted away. I began to reflect on how financially comfortable I was last month, to the extent that I had already programmed everything to continue like that at least till the end of the year. I was paying for things with ease. A lot of expenses that I never planned for came up during that period, and there was always money to sort them out without thinking much about it.

But along the line everything changed.

_\

_ I wished the earnings continued. My mind ran far trying to question some happenings in this life.

After my mind returned, I smiled and still thanked God for everything because I have things I did with the money, and it wasn’t a waste. The only issue was that the flow stopped and killed my dream of becoming a millionaire within a year if it had continued. But it’s still okay, because nothing lasts forever.

Thanks for reading.

_The photo used is mine_

body.title: ЄС оновив правила в’їзду з домашніми тваринами
body.body:
![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWHoMczsy4B1LdbNUwsSSyeBc22pLeGFSskkSmZu7BsBk/image)

З 22 квітня 2026 року в Євросоюзі чинні оновлені правила перевезення домашніх собак, котів і тхорів. 

Європейські паспорти для тварин надалі видаватимуть лише тим, хто постійно проживає в ЄС. Сезонні відвідувачі або власники житла для відпочинку в ЄС втрачають право на отримання документа.

Для перевезення тварин у межах ЄС та для в'їзду з третіх країн необхідні:
1. Обов'язковий мікрочіп; чіпування зробити до щеплення від сказу або того ж дня.
2. Вакцинація проти сказу.
3. Єдиний європейський паспорт.
4. Одна особа може перевозити не більше п'яти тварин (або підтвердити участь у змаганнях, виставках тощо).
Для в'їзду до деяких країн залишається обов'язковою обробка собак від глистів.

Для в'їзду до ЄС з третіх країн (включно з Україною), потрібний європейський сертифікат здоров'я тварини, виданий принаймні за 10 днів до прибуття. Додатково може знадобитися FAVN-тест. 

Експерти радять заздалегідь уточнювати у ветеринара точні вимоги країни призначення.

body.title: Is chainsaw legal in India?
body.body:
![Is chainsaw legal in India (1).jpg](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/2c54355b1e8e47000d19d314d313fba205ae729b88823e0f941e7069045e2016)



Yes, chainsaws are legal in India, but their use is regulated under certain laws. Owning a chainsaw for personal, agricultural, or commercial purposes is generally allowed. Farmers, gardeners, and woodworkers commonly use a [petrol chainsaw for farming](https://www.chandakagro.com/product/electric-and-petrol-chainsaw) for cutting wood, pruning trees, and land maintenance. There is no specific ban on purchasing or owning a chainsaw in India.

However, restrictions apply when it comes to cutting trees. Under the Indian Forest Act, 1927 and various state-level tree preservation laws, you cannot cut trees—especially in forest areas or protected zones-without proper permission from local authorities. Even on private land, some states require approval before felling certain types of trees.

Using a chainsaw irresponsibly, such as for illegal logging or damaging public property, can lead to fines or legal action. Safety is also important, and users should follow proper handling guidelines to avoid accidents.

In summary, chainsaws are legal tools in India, but their usage must comply with forestry and environmental regulations. Always check local rules before cutting trees.

body.title: And…Windows - April 27, 2026@goldenoakfarm
body.body:
![Prepping for windows collage text crop April 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/23z7MyErKixcWGkbKrULiRR2U4Zmo5oL1Pd4bJHsB7R17jCnXERzQ8sQGypa1cXwNWZi4.jpg)

On Monday morning I was up at 5:30AM and got started on my post. I had to stop around 7AM to start prepping for windows. I got the kitchen cleaned up, got out the back porch screens and went out and started emptying out the back porch.

![Stuff from bathroom window washed crop April 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/EoeEvhZ56uG8i3VojcuufZZPmHKruW9d5dzzcaGpF4kNFu4wgSTARuYtoarfMDZ21xS.jpg)

Once everything was out of the windows there, I went to the bathroom and started emptying that window. Next was the clean room window. I sat down for a while then got up and washed up all the things from the bathroom.

And then I got the phone call just after 8AM, the window washer wasn’t coming at all this week. He was rescheduled for next week. Well, wasn’t that grand! I had the house all torn up, ready to do windows. I wasn’t leaving it like that for a week. Sigh… So I sat down and finished my post and then got started.

The plan had been, because it was a lovely day, to get as many of the outside windows done as we could. That meant the washer on a ladder and me inside. Well…

![Doing outside windows crop April 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/23tvgfEewvVLLMyNdbcDSo2MRt64BHge34VSU9PMwzrLfK9zpJPJL4vrmVHtw2Roxpk1X.jpg)

So I decided I would do the outsides and the insides by myself. So I got the ladder and carefully set it up at each window and got the outsides done by 10AM.

![Doing bathroom window crop April 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/EpCAKXhx6iob6XD1p65wgv3pV8JaeS6JJLKue3E1YMGgH3sTcDbbHitzgrj2z6LcABe.jpg)

I got the stuff put away from the outside and sat down for a while. Then around 11AM I got started on the inside. I did the bathroom first as the sun was on it and things wouldn’t get better. Then the clean room window and I stopped for lunch and a rest.

I got a call from the Senior center that the van was coming early for the event, so I got right up and got a shower and got ready. I had time to put some of the stuff back into the bathroom window.

![Wildlife April 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/23vshuV4BH7c33gNQifpGenzW1bDGUT9ziU7wDaTbQcAUayu8KmhhbNcdHW5MZjh1Cri1.jpg)

I had time when I got to the Senior center to chat with the presenter. She had prepared an excellent Powerpoint, but in was brought in through a browser and the Senior center’s internet leaves a bit to be desired. All her cool videos would not play, just sat buffering. She was so disappointed. But the still photos were cool too and she had a lot of interesting things she had seen from her kayak on the river.

![Back porch - putting it all back crop April 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/23xp8qr7G4Cn3DCxyGKwwbwHwbTLvm8sD58BP4ByksMMtuk294fV2hskqy5AqBDRnbz6X.jpg)

Once I was back home, I sat down for a while then went out and got the insides of the back porch windows washed and put all the shelving back up and moved the plants back. I finished about 5PM.

So I spent the rest of the day on the couch watching ‘Leave It to Beaver’ until I had to pull shades at 8PM. My son would light the fires during the night when the temps dropped.

On Tuesday I need to clean up the kitchen and get seedlings watered or fed. When my helper friend arrives at 10:30AM we have to feed the seedlings in the cold frame. I’m hoping to take some of the ones in the house to the cold frame as they have gotten too big to be under lights. 

It’s still to be 40’s at night for another 10 days so I hope they will be ok. I’m tired of the plastic on the cold frame and am debating taking it off now. We have lots of chores to get done and I’d like to think I could get out to gardens later. I have some that are in the shade on the north side of the house that could sure use cleaning out.

![Mini bio framed Jan 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/23xyn876JURgHHjsp757ZTvXeEEBjdDeLXWynRcLCeuqwPPsqtEtXTosSPyKZdAgWivJB.jpg)

body.title: 😅 Ese “penalti” que nunca debí patear ⚽ [ Esp - Eng ] 😅 That “penalty” I should have never taken ⚽
body.body:
>

Feliz martes para toda esta hermosa comunidad de #EmpowerTalent. Un abrazo para cada uno, y un agradecimiento especial a @angelica7 por su constancia y por mantener este espacio lleno de motivación semana tras semana.

Esta semana, cuando leí el tema *“Travesuras”*, no pude evitar sonreír… porque aunque siempre fui un muchacho tranquilo y aplicado, hubo momentos donde también me tocó vivir situaciones que hoy recuerdo y me dan risa. De esas travesuras que en su momento parecían un problema grande, pero que con el tiempo se convierten en historias que uno cuenta entre risas.

Y créanme, hubo una en particular que todavía, cuando la recuerdo, no sé si reírme o decir: ***¿en qué estaba pensando?***
________

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPhgVaepKQdCHi1jnqpe2sdz2bfjpHqvj3CwBf1jnvhP6/image.png)</center>

<center>*\

*</center>

________

Desde muy pequeño fui un muchacho aplicado, de esos que estudian, cumplen con sus tareas y sin darse cuenta terminan destacando en el salón. Eso me daba ciertos privilegios con los profesores, pero también hacía que mis compañeros me vieran diferente. Aun así, yo tenía algo muy claro: mi pasión era el fútbol. Desde niño me moría por jugar a la pelota, en el colegio, en la calle, donde fuera. Apenas salía de clases agarraba mis cosas y me iba directo al campo que me quedaba a pocos metros de mi casa. Ese era mi mundo, ahí me olvidaba de todo. Ahí no era el aplicado del salón, era el que quería patear, correr y disfrutar.
________

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbD61NN56x8nfaBDS8xmxUtP1qfEda7mFSQLTHvpKn7MF/image.png)</center>

<center>*\

*</center>
________

Recuerdo esos tiempos en Venezuela, mi amada patria. Yo estaba en 4to grado de educación primaria, en la escuela de la Urbanización San Esteban, en Puerto Cabello, Carabobo. Allí, en los colegios públicos donde estudiábamos muchos muchachos de bajos recursos, el Estado nos garantizaba algo tan importante como la alimentación. Nos daban nuestra merienda: un vaso de leche, a veces en cartón, otras en vasitos plásticos, con una empanada o un sándwich de jamón y queso. Era algo sencillo, pero para nosotros era mucho. Era parte del día, parte de lo normal. Hoy uno lo piensa y dice: éramos ricos y no lo sabíamos. Todo era más tranquilo, más sano, más inocente.
________

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeBSY3zG6VFMSDzCQBAjZQZ4sHVgqzX4jJmU7qsE8HJ2h/image.png)</center>

<center>*\

*</center>
________

Pero claro, como todo salón de clases, cuando la maestra no estaba eso se descontrolaba. Ese día la profesora había bajado a la dirección y el salón estaba vuelto un relajo. Cada quien en lo suyo, unos hablando, otros corriendo, y muchos jugando con los potes de leche vacíos como si fuera un futbolito improvisado. Y ahí fue donde empezó la travesura, pero no mía, sino de mis compañeros.

A alguien se le ocurrió aprovecharse de lo mucho que me gustaba el fútbol. Me pusieron un vaso en el suelo, haciéndome creer que estaba vacío. Yo, inocente, me dejé llevar. Me perfilé como si fuera a cobrar un penalti en una final. Me paré firme, tomé impulso y lo pateé con fe, pero lo que vino después fue una tragedia. Ese vaso no estaba vacío, tenía leche todavía. Eso no fue un penal, eso fue un desastre. La leche salió por todos lados, bañó el pizarrón, el escritorio de la maestra, y lo peor es que había documentos ahí. El salón se vino abajo de la risa, y yo me quería morir. Ahí entendí algo que no se me olvida: no todo lo que parece penal se patea.
________

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcEkpxgfrocGKqxnqJKn2f9oPhNJMyDxeY7jroVQ8G2GF/image.png)</center>

<center>*\

*</center>
_______

No dio tiempo de hacer nada. A los pocos minutos llegó la maestra, vio el desastre y castigó a todo el salón. Nos quedamos sin recreo ese día, todos sentados sin hablar. Pero conmigo no quedó ahí. Me llevaron a la dirección, llamaron a mi representante y bueno, lo demás es historia. La paliza que me dio mi papá con la correa de cuero todavía la recuerdo. Ahí se me acabó el partido.
_________

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPqKLCFKj1NMiUP5ysYxEVkkTP2xR84tvdytTRqcSSvGM/image.png)</center>

<center>*\

*</center>
________

Hoy lo recuerdo y me da risa. En ese momento fue un problema grande, pero ahora es una anécdota. Eran otros tiempos, una infancia sana, sin redes sociales, donde había que inventar para distraerse, donde las travesuras eran parte de crecer. Todo era más simple, más real.

Y al final uno entiende que esas cosas también forman parte de lo que somos hoy. Son recuerdos que te sacan una sonrisa y te llevan a esa época donde todo era más ligero. Hoy uno ya no hace esas travesuras, pero sí puede volver a esa sensación. Porque dentro de cada adulto siempre queda ese niño, el que un día se perfiló y pateó algo que no debía.

<center>![SeparadorHive.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mballesteros/23t7YWoN53XUARh93PVvS9mqaVjjjMGSNi6uJUMjKptGwBVoiTyadsRVjRPAE27xgxsc7.png)</center>

Y al final, uno entiende que esas travesuras no solo eran momentos de locura, también eran parte de crecer, de aprender y de vivir una infancia que hoy se recuerda con una sonrisa. En ese momento parecía el fin del mundo, pero hoy es una historia que vale la pena contar.

Ahora te pregunto: ***¿cuál fue esa travesura que nunca olvidaste? ¿Eras de los tranquilos o de los que siempre estaban metidos en algo?***

Gracias por llegar hasta aquí. Te leo en la caja de comentarios. Un abrazo grande para todos.
____

body.title: The cold front landed overnight.
body.body:
I mentioned in yesterday's post that we were expecting a new cold front.
![008.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23xKvdAHpNAdScVvQfDg5pogL6DxQ8KozMsF8gLKCFK3HKggRnJF4DFGfeVospxeBqiAL.jpg)

This shot above was the only early morning sun that we saw for the whole day.

The rest of the day was covered with water, and we were thoroughly soaked by the rain on our walk to the church. I have to say that the rain fell intermittently and one had to be careful not to mistime the breaks in the rain. For instance, a break would arrive and one would go outside only to walk into a smattering of rainfall by a roving raincloud. Best is to keep an eye for the light grey sky with no darker clouds hanging around during a break in the rain.

Come with us for a quick drive, and in the second part of the post I will show you what was waiting for us when we arrived back home.  

Three shots below of the drive in the rain. 
![011.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EqUdSQyrogsw4xkQLZ1QdtKfRKQis2zCLeYCLyLJBXKDasWJStLA3dPZLGsdfe4g58g.JPG)

![012.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/243LzwM7GAfHCykkSUE6ppiUiVHmMoUsiEqBb8CZBnUnzzbgnDwiMn76GXa563AjtqCVc.JPG)

![016.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EqUcx7Br5uY7FaqbTE8rjLESqQqrZkN7Us61zcqaUmHsxHktfdJAWra24pFFQgXxaXq.JPG)

Right, now let me show you some shots back at home. 

A shot below of a Speckled Pigeon to show you how they handle the rain.
![026.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23w2sMRDMcRcgNzh6dzM3UfiFn3fRdUgDZMz2SuhZeinrCV9qhSMYnA5dYDSd4cTwFf5L.JPG)

I am sure that the squirrels watch out for our car, as we had hardly arrived back when they scurried up to the study window to tell me that they want food. It is always like this, but on this day the other wildlife was nowhere to be seen. Not even a little bird, or a full complement of squirrels as only two young females arrived.

My wife places the peanuts next to the two water bowls so that they don't fight.
![018.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EoGzKZfH7h9Kf18u6grmWhgGTgsYeYbFURbQvYC276pqi7hbThN5Poa7BRbY9QmDCd3.JPG)

So, the one eats at the bowl at the bottom, and the other one grabs a nut at the top bowl and then jumps up on the wall to eat it. 
![019.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23uFTrLXkaa18stz6YNQ5f7gLUKvtM2LPmSF4XfcPYtCGNkPkzHt8Y8BMZPpk28bTnBfB.JPG)

Tail umbrella time, as a soft rain was falling. 
![023.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EoK6NhPfzouumrDus8mx4C328L7EmVMrWfVpMmEiH1dnHvrFfyknP7W17QigJFvKQ2Y.JPG)

This one was wetter than the other one. 
![021.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/Ep1YKSDbmXxrAEVKbHntgeNKcXnUSzXWYkXMzdC8nv55Y8LPyiEeihvuVTRNHatjzsn.JPG)

Finally, here is a close-up of the wet one. 
![029.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EowG5BPmgYmBEdiG1RswBMXMW4dJe599ksuR5M9MgVy3dvzLKDh7QmKEQgmdNzXQ1Jq.JPG)

Then you just have to see when the squirrels have had enough to eat, and then they start to bury the remaining nuts on the sidewalks in the mud. Normally their faces are cloaked in mud, and they almost look like racoons.  But they don't mind as when they have buried all of the nuts, they rinse their faces in the rain puddles next to the road. Then they sit preening themselves like the birds. 

Autumn has decided to resign here, as the winter rains and cold have arrived instead. We are already down to a cold daytime maximum of 14C temperature, and in other areas in the country they have dropped to 8C. Some people walk around dressed like Eskimos, as the quick change from the high temperatures in Summer to these low temperatures is difficult to cope with. But we are all survivors.
Such is life.

I hope you enjoyed the pictures and the story. 

Photos by Zac Smith. All-Rights-Reserved.

Camera: Canon PowershotSX70HS Bridge camera.

Thank you kindly for supporting this post.

body.title: A distinctive rural atmosphere with tranquility and natural views that are a treat for the eyes.
body.body:
>

Hello, my friends, as usual, I hope you are all healthy and happy, allowing you to carry out your daily activities smoothly. I hope you all have a wonderful day.

In this meeting, I return to this beloved community to share some random images depicting the atmosphere in my village with all of you in this beloved community. The village is known for its uniquely peaceful atmosphere and pristine open nature.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQkgywn6CyWzkfgSkc7izk2aoark4LHd988HwRaVjXY3V/img_20260424_wa0041.jpg

Rural areas are known for their tranquil atmosphere and unique customs. The scenery and geography of the villages also offer stunning views. Another interesting aspect is the social solidarity, where village life is synonymous with mutual cooperation and stronger social ties than in cities.

This image was taken after a mutual cooperation event we held at our village's Meunasah (traditional mosque). It's important to note that the Meunasah is the center of community, worship, and traditional religious education in every village in Aceh.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcYG4pqfQDwCDLoAzYTX5fY2xwaZ9dXHvk56i7oBkzcPy/img_20260424_wa0042.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVXYhf2bKL6VmK87PY6jDabBBZiNdRTjaVXtftgGh7MCj/img_20260424_wa0035.jpg)

Next, I also had the chance to enjoy the atmosphere in the swamp area. This swamp is a unique, naturally formed wetland ecosystem that is often flooded, both permanently and seasonally. I personally observed that the swamp in our area always has water, even during the dry season.

This area used to be my favorite place to play with my friends as a child.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUHu7fWcxxvvWbPyUD1Bfg2vtYEq6cXDXm4HUFrGaGcSk/img_20260424_wa0036.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSWzoSW8VEeuKkL6rqKXM3hVbBcrqPap882YB6ZYCvjLv/img_20260424_wa0038.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQ7LzFwURQv84mCLcRjHHRR8boZ1N6tFiEwKVZFvrXVMa/img_20260424_wa0039.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVs2Hpare4KuV7tHkxiBGsNySXeadARkA11R2aqrXdpnG/img_20260424_wa0040.jpg)
